planned\">follow-on</span></td></tr>\n          </tbody>\n        </table>\n\n        <div data-demo=\"routingExplorer\"></div>\n\n        <p><strong>Branch-level fan-out</strong>: for <code>comparator</code> / <code>iterator</code> / etc., each branch port acts like a small plain output of its own. If the comparator's <code>lt</code> port has three wires going to three consumers, then on every invocation where the routing decision picks <code>lt</code>, all three of those wires fire. The routing decision picks <em>which branch</em>; fan-out picks <em>which consumers</em> on that branch receive the value.</p>\n\n        <p>Plain output port can fan freely too — multiple connections from <code>from_branch: null</code> send copies to every wired consumer. Pulling multiple wires from a single output is not a routing decision.</p>\n\n        <div data-demo=\"weighted\"></div>\n\n        <h3 id=\"ports\">Input ports</h3>\n<pre data-lang=\"json\">\"inputs\": [\n  { \"name\": \"text\",        \"type\": \"string\" },\n  { \"name\": \"config_path\", \"type\": \"string\", \"optional\": true,\n    \"value\": \"config.json\" }\n]</pre>\n        <p>Every input port is in one of three states at compile time:</p>\n        <ol>\n          <li>A wire is connected to it.</li>\n          <li>A literal <code>value</code> is set on it.</li>\n          <li>It carries <code>optional: true</code>.</li>\n        </ol>\n        <p><strong>Compile fails</strong> when any port is in none of those states. The error is precise: which box, which port. Enforced at the Compile button (phase 2 UI / phase 3 build) and again in the C graph loader at runtime — belt and suspenders against hand-edited maps.</p>\n\n        <div class=\"callout\">\n          <strong>Optional ≠ null. </strong><code>optional: true</code> does not mean &ldquo;pass null&rdquo; — it means the argument doesn't have to be passed. The dispatch layer assembles <code>input_data[]</code> / <code>input_sizes[]</code> from the slots that actually have values; an absent optional port shortens <code>n_inputs</code> by one and the language's native short-arg convention handles the rest.\n        </div>\n\n        <p>Null as an <strong>explicit</strong> value (typed <code>null</code> into the literal field) is a different thing: it arrives through the function call as a real argument, mapped to the language's native null (Lua <code>nil</code>, Bash empty string <code>\"\"</code>, C <code>NULL</code>).</p>\n\n        <h3 id=\"connections\">Connections</h3>\n        <p>Connections are written to <strong>both</strong> endpoint box files. The loader validates at load time that both ends agree — disagreement is a hard error.</p>\n<pre data-lang=\"json\">{ \"from_box\": \"...\",\n  \"from_branch\": null | \"lt\" | \"eq\" | \"gt\" | \"out_0\" | ...,\n  \"to_box\":   \"...\",\n  \"to_input\": \"...\" }</pre>\n        <p><code>from_branch</code> is <code>null</code> for <code>routing: plain</code> and for boxes without a routing field; otherwise it names the branch port the wire leaves from.</p>\n\n        <h2 id=\"specs\">Language spec system (phase 3)</h2>\n        <p>Each language is a <strong>spec</strong> — a <code>.so</code> library at <code>langs/&lt;name&gt;/spec.so</code> that exports a <code>lang_spec_t</code> symbol. The pool runner loads every <code>langs/*/spec.so</code> at startup via <code>dlopen</code> and registers it by <code>name</code> (for box lookup) and <code>file_ext</code> (for source resolution). The spec contract is uniform across languages; no language is privileged. The runner itself does not link to liblua, libc++, or any language-specific runtime — only specs do.</p>\n\n        <h3 id=\"spec-struct\">lang_spec_t</h3>\n<pre data-lang=\"c\">typedef struct {\n    const char *name;       // \"lua\", \"bash\", \"c\", \"python\", ...\n    const char *file_ext;   // \".lua\", \".sh\", \".c\", \".py\"\n\n    // Once-per-worker. Pool startup calls init() for every spec on\n    // every worker before unblocking the init barrier; teardown()\n    // runs at shutdown.\n    void *(*init)    (int worker_idx);\n    void  (*teardown)(void *handle);\n\n    // Optional: at map-compile time. C uses this to gcc -shared -fPIC.\n    // Lua and Bash leave this NULL.\n    int   (*compile) (const char *src_path, const char *out_path);\n\n    // Universal invoke path: JSON bytes in, JSON bytes out.\n    // Used across every cross-language wire.\n    int   (*invoke_json)  (void *handle, /* common args */);\n\n    // Fast invoke path: language-native bytes in, language-native bytes out.\n    // Used when producer and consumer share a language.\n    int   (*invoke_native)(void *handle, /* common args */);\n\n    // Bridges used when a value crosses a language boundary.\n    int   (*native_to_json)(...);\n    int   (*json_to_native)(...);\n} lang_spec_t;\n\nextern lang_spec_t soramech_lang_spec;</pre>\n        <p>A nonzero return from <code>invoke_*</code> is a fatal error. The dispatch layer prints the context (box id, function name, language) and aborts. No recovery, no retry, no per-task \"failed\" state. Bugs do not belong in production.</p>\n\n        <h3 id=\"init-barrier\">Init barrier</h3>\n        <p>Workers are not safe to dispatch to until every worker has completed <code>init</code> for every spec the map uses. Pool startup runs each worker's <code>init</code> calls, increments a shared <code>workers_ready</code> atomic, and blocks on a condition variable. The main thread waits for <code>workers_ready == n_workers</code>, then broadcasts — all workers release together and begin pulling tasks. One-shot; doesn't re-engage.</p>\n\n        <h3 id=\"fast-path\">Same-language wire fast path</h3>\n        <p>Wire format defaults to JSON. At compile time, every wire is classified <code>fast_path: true</code> (same language at both ends) or <code>false</code> (crosses a language boundary). The compile step also records the producer's <code>output_format</code> per box — <code>native</code> if <strong>all</strong> consumers of its output share its language, <code>json</code> if any consumer is different.</p>\n\n        <p>Per-language native forms:</p>\n        <ul>\n          <li><strong>Lua</strong> — <code>lua_dump</code> for closures, <code>cjson</code> or msgpack for tables, raw bytes for strings/numbers.</li>\n          <li><strong>C</strong> — <code>memcpy</code> of the typed struct (the C spec's <code>compile</code> callback knows the types).</li>\n          <li><strong>Bash</strong> — strings only; the fast path is an alias of the JSON path.</li>\n        </ul>\n\n        <h3 id=\"shipped-specs\">Shipped specs</h3>\n        <p><code>langs/lua/spec.so</code>, <code>langs/c/spec.so</code>, <code>langs/bash/spec.so</code> ship as reference implementations:</p>\n        <ul>\n          <li><strong>Lua</strong> — <code>init</code> constructs a <code>lua_State</code>; <code>invoke_*</code> does <code>luaL_loadfile</code> (cached) + <code>lua_pcall</code>.</li>\n          <li><strong>C</strong> — <code>compile</code> runs <code>gcc -shared -fPIC -o &lt;out&gt; &lt;src&gt;</code> (caching by mtime); <code>invoke_*</code> does <code>dlsym</code> + direct call through a wrapper the compile step generates from the box signature.</li>\n          <li><strong>Bash</strong> — <code>init</code> spawns a persistent bash subprocess and connects to it over a Unix domain socket. <code>invoke_*</code> sends a framed request, reads a framed response. The same shape every future non-embeddable-runtime language uses.</li>\n        </ul>\n        <p>A user adds a new language by writing a <code>langs/&lt;name&gt;/spec.c</code> and a small Makefile. SoraMech itself does not transpile box source between languages.</p>\n\n        <h2 id=\"exec-2\">Execution model — phase 2 (synchronous)</h2>\n        <p>The runner walks the graph depth-first from the boxes that have all their inputs satisfied. Each box call:</p>\n        <ol>\n          <li>Read wired output values from predecessor boxes.</li>\n          <li>Shell out to the appropriate driver script (<code>drivers/&lt;lang&gt;.sh</code>).</li>\n          <li>Decode the single JSON value from driver stdout.</li>\n          <li>Hold the output in runner memory, keyed by box id.</li>\n          <li>Fire connections — enqueue boxes whose inputs are now met.</li>\n        </ol>\n        <p>Single-threaded; one process per box call. The <code>task_fn</code> boundary matches the phase 3 dispatch action signature, so the executor can be swapped without changing the box execution model.</p>\n\n        <h2 id=\"exec-3\">Execution model — phase 3 (thread pool)</h2>\n        <p>Tasks are ephemeral; box state is durable. Each box owns one slot per input port plus optional state (iterator counter, language handle). A <strong>task</strong> is one stack frame on a worker — <code>box_id</code> is all it carries. Tasks come and go; boxes persist for the run.</p>\n\n        <h3 id=\"slots\">Slots</h3>\n        <p>Every input port has exactly one slot, allocated at graph load and freed at run end. A wire is a routing declaration; the producer doesn't own a slot — its output is a push event into every downstream input slot it's wired to. Fan-out is N pushes; fan-in is N producers pushing into one slot.</p>\n\n        <table>\n          <thead><tr><th>Mode</th><th>Cells</th><th>Reads via</th><th>Used for</th></tr></thead>\n          <tbody>\n            <tr><td>1-cell peek</td>           <td>1</td>     <td><code>slot_peek</code></td>      <td>Literals; wires from runs-once producers</td></tr>\n            <tr><td>N-cell pop</td>            <td>N</td>     <td><code>slot_pop</code></td>       <td>Wires whose producer runs many times</td></tr>\n            <tr><td><code>SLOT_ATOMIC_COUNTER</code></td><td>1 atom</td><td><code>slot_read_inc</code></td><td>Iterator / randomizer / weighted counters</td></tr>\n          </tbody>\n        </table>\n\n        <div data-demo=\"slotStore\"></div>\n\n        <p>Compile-time analysis decides per wire: a producer is &ldquo;runs-once&rdquo; if no transitive ancestor is an iterator, else &ldquo;runs-N-times.&rdquo; The former gets a 1-cell peek slot (subsequent consumer tasks re-read the same value); the latter gets an N-cell ring (FIFO drain, one cell per consumer task).</p>\n        <p>Variable-size payloads (long LLM outputs, dynamically-sized arrays) live in a separate <strong>large-value heap</strong>. The slot then holds a small fixed-size handle <code>{ uint32_t size; uint32_t offset; }</code>. The slot allocator only ever sees fixed-size slots; the two-tier scheme keeps the hot path simple while supporting unbounded values.</p>\n\n        <h3 id=\"tagging\">Cell tagging for parallel iterators</h3>\n        <p>Each cell optionally carries a 4-byte ordering tag alongside its data. Iterator pushes carry their counter value as the tag; slots downstream of an iterator are allocated with <code>SLOT_TAGGED</code>, and <code>slot_pop</code> on a tagged slot returns the <strong>lowest-tag</strong> cell — not the head. This preserves iteration order across parallel iterator workers.</p>\n\n        <div data-demo=\"cellTagging\"></div>\n\n        <p>When a consumer has two tagged inputs from two iterators, each port pops in tag order independently — pairing falls out as <code>(A_K, B_K)</code> for every K.</p>\n\n        <h3 id=\"dispatch-action\">The dispatch action</h3>\n        <p>One C function, one phase per worker per task:</p>\n        <ol>\n          <li><strong>Read inputs.</strong> For each input port: <code>slot_peek</code> (peek mode) or <code>slot_pop</code> (pop mode) into a heap buffer. Tasks are spawned only when every input slot has a value (spawn-on-input-ready rule), so no waiting is needed.</li>\n          <li><strong>Invoke spec.</strong> Look up the box's <code>lang</code>, find the worker's handle for it, call <code>invoke_native</code> or <code>invoke_json</code> (per the wire's fast-path classification).</li>\n          <li><strong>Pick the branch.</strong> Dispatch on <code>routing.kind</code>: plain (fan to all), comparator (compare to comparand), iterator (atomic counter read), randomizer / weighted / distributor (kind-specific rule).</li>\n          <li><strong>Push.</strong> For each firing wire, <code>slot_push</code> into the consumer's input slot. The push carries the appropriate ordering tag. Each push triggers a spawn-on-input-ready check on the consumer.</li>\n          <li><strong>Done.</strong> The action returns; the pool decrements the active-task counter. The action does not block, does not wait, does not park.</li>\n        </ol>\n\n        <div data-demo=\"iterator\"></div>\n\n        <h3 id=\"startup\">Startup, quiescence, termination</h3>\n        <p><strong>Startup:</strong> the pool runner pushes literal-input values into the corresponding slots, then spawns first tasks for boxes whose input sets are now satisfied. Iterator counter slots start at 0.</p>\n        <p><strong>Quiescence:</strong> the main thread waits on a condition variable that signals when the pool's active-task counter reaches zero with no pending spawns. That's the run-over signal. The graph validator at load time rejects non-iterator cycles, so the run cannot deadlock — an iterator with no upstream pushes simply contributes nothing further, and once the counter drains, termination fires.</p>\n        <p><strong>Hard-crash error policy:</strong> a nonzero <code>invoke_*</code> return aborts the process. No retry, no per-task failed state, no fallback executor.</p>\n\n        <h3 id=\"blocking\">Blocking-aware iterator pattern</h3>\n        <p>Long-running operations (network calls, LLM inference) hold their worker for the duration. Pool size is the budget. The cooperative pattern for not holding a worker for minutes: split the call into a &ldquo;kickoff&rdquo; box and a &ldquo;check-done&rdquo; iterator that polls. Each pass through the iterator releases the worker between checks. Documented fully in <a href=\"004-ipc-and-threading.html\">§ 04 · IPC & Threading</a>.</p>\n\n        <h2 id=\"run-output\">Run output — <code>tmp/last-run.jsonl</code></h2>\n        <p>Phase 3 writes one JSON object per event, one event per line. The format decouples the runner from the editor — the editor never displays run results; the file is for LLM consumption, CLI viewers, and the integration test harness.</p>\n<pre data-lang=\"jsonl\">{\"event\":\"run_start\", \"ts\":..., \"map\":\"maps/&lt;name&gt;\", \"n_workers\":16}\n{\"event\":\"task_submit\", \"ts\":..., \"task_id\":42, \"box_id\":\"classify\"}\n{\"event\":\"task_start\",  \"ts\":..., \"task_id\":42, \"worker_idx\":3}\n{\"event\":\"task_end\",    \"ts\":..., \"task_id\":42, \"duration_us\":127, \"output_size\":12}\n{\"event\":\"slot_alloc\",  \"ts\":..., \"slot_id\":5, \"size\":256, \"n_cells\":1}   // SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1\n{\"event\":\"slot_free\",   \"ts\":..., \"slot_id\":5}                              // SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1\n{\"event\":\"run_end\",     \"ts\":..., \"duration_us\":1850, \"n_tasks\":7}</pre>\n        <p><strong>Mechanism:</strong> a dedicated writer thread drains a multi-producer single-consumer ring buffer of fixed-size event records, serializes each to JSON, and appends to the file. Workers push records into the ring without contending on a file mutex. The writer joins before <code>pool_destroy</code>, including a final <code>run_end</code> summary.</p>\n        <p>Inputs/outputs per task are off by default (<code>SORAMECH_LOG_VALUES=1</code> to enable; truncated past 4 KB). Slot allocator events are off by default (<code>SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1</code>). Timestamps are Unix epoch floats. The file is overwritten on every run.</p>\n\n        <h2 id=\"build\">Build & compile pipeline</h2>\n        <p>A top-level <code>Makefile</code> builds:</p>\n        <ol>\n          <li><code>soramech-pool</code> — statically links the pool, JSON parser, slot store, graph loader, dispatch layer, spec registry.</li>\n          <li><code>langs/&lt;name&gt;/spec.so</code> — per-spec, via the per-language Makefile (Lua links LuaJIT; C links <code>-ldl</code>; Bash links nothing extra).</li>\n        </ol>\n        <p>Modes: <code>make</code> (release, <code>-O2 -Wall</code>), <code>make DEBUG=1</code> (<code>-O0 -g</code>), <code>make STRICT=1</code> (release + <code>-Werror -Wextra -Wpedantic</code>).</p>\n        <p>Vendored dependencies (the task pool, the JSON parser) live under <code>libs/</code> as plain source — no submodules, no fetches at build time.</p>\n        <p>Spec discovery at runtime: the runner reads <code>/proc/self/exe</code>, follows the symlink, and scans for <code>langs/</code> next to its own binary. <code>SORAMECH_LANGS_DIR=/path/to/langs</code> overrides for development.</p>\n\n        <h3 id=\"compile-pkg\">Compile a map for standalone execution</h3>\n        <p><code>./compiled/pool-runner</code> runs a map independently of the editor and the surrounding source tree. The compile step (Compile button in the editor, or <code>soramech-compile &lt;map-dir&gt;</code> from the CLI) produces:</p>\n<pre data-lang=\"layout\">maps/&lt;name&gt;/compiled/\n  pool-runner          ← copy or symlink of soramech-pool\n  src/                 ← every source file the map uses\n  bin/                 ← per-box compiled .so files (C boxes)\n  langs/&lt;name&gt;/spec.so ← one per language the map uses\n  manifest.json        ← every box, its language, artifact path, build version</pre>\n        <p>Steps: walk the graph (reusing the C loader's validation); copy source files and transitive <code>require</code> / <code>#include</code> dependencies; invoke each spec's <code>compile</code> callback for boxes whose language needs it; copy the spec <code>.so</code> files used by the map; copy or symlink the runner binary; write the manifest. Per-box artifacts mtime-compare so a re-compile recompiles only what changed. Any failure aborts the step and leaves the partial output for inspection but does not write the manifest, so the deployment is recognizably broken until a clean compile succeeds.</p>\n\n        <h2 id=\"data-files\">Data files</h2>\n        <p>Persistent data lives in <code>data/&lt;name&gt;.json</code> and is accessed via <code>libs/soramech-data.lua</code> (<code>data.get</code> / <code>data.set</code> / <code>data.load</code>). Format:</p>\n<pre data-lang=\"json\">{\n  \"constant\": false,\n  \"fields\": {\n    \"history\": [],\n    \"config\": { \"constant\": true,\n                \"value\": { \"model\": \"soramind-default\" } }\n  }\n}</pre>\n        <p>Top-level <code>constant: true</code> makes the whole file read-only; field-level <code>constant</code> flags individual fields within an otherwise mutable file. This is <strong>separate</strong> from the <code>data</code> box kind (which reads arbitrary files at the dispatch layer).</p>\n        <p>Ephemeral state (scratch tables, run logs, <code>last-run.jsonl</code>) goes to <code>tmp/</code>, a symlink to <code>/tmp/&lt;map-name&gt;/</code>. Survives the run but not a reboot — intentionally.</p>\n\n        <div class=\"page-nav\">\n          <a href=\"index.html\"><span class=\"dir\">◂ back</span><span class=\"title\">Contents</span></a>\n          <a href=\"002-roadmap.html\" class=\"next\"><span class=\"dir\">next ▸</span><span class=\"title\">Roadmap</span></a>\n        </div>\n      </div>\n    </main>\n  </div>\n</body>\n</html>\n",
  "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/docs/HTML/001-architecture.html"
}

Each box invocation shells out to a driver script, which starts a new process, runs the function, and exits. The return value passes through stdout. The <code>task_fn</code> boundary swaps in the thread pool. Worker threads pull tasks from the pool; OS-level scheduling replaces any single-threaded ordering. They live for the entire run.</p>\n\n        <h3 id=\"blocking-states\">Blocking and unblocking — pointer-only transitions</h3>\n        <p>When a task cannot run (upstream output not yet available), it is placed in its upstream task's waiting list. This is a pointer move — no allocation, no struct copy. The task struct stays exactly where it is.</p>\n        <p>When an upstream task completes and writes its return value to shared memory, it walks its waiting list and re-adds each entry to the main task queue. Again, a pointer move only. The unblocked task's struct is unchanged; only its position in the queue changes.</p>\n        <p>This means &ldquo;blocked&rdquo;, &ldquo;queued&rdquo;, and &ldquo;running&rdquo; are states defined by which list a task's pointer currently lives in — not by any field in the struct.</p>\n\n        <h3 id=\"per-thread-runtimes\">Per-thread language runtimes</h3>\n        <p>Each worker thread initializes its own language runtimes at startup:</p>\n        <ul>\n          <li><strong>Lua:</strong> one <code>lua_State</code> per thread. Lua states are not thread-safe, but one per thread requires no locking. The task wrapper calls the box function via <code>lua_pcall</code>.</li>\n          <li><strong>C:</strong> the compiled box function is called directly through the function pointer. No interpreter, no overhead beyond the call itself.</li>\n          <li><strong>Bash/other:</strong> a persistent subprocess per thread (Unix domain socket server model — see Option 3 below). The task wrapper sends a request and blocks the thread waiting for the response.</li>\n        </ul>\n\n        <h3 id=\"iterator-requeue\">Iterator self-re-queue</h3>\n        <p>An iterator task does not terminate after one invocation. When it completes:</p>\n        <ol>\n          <li>It increments its <code>counter</code> field in-place (or wraps to 0).</li>\n          <li>It checks its input queue for the next pending value.</li>\n          <li>If a value is waiting: it updates its input pointer and re-adds itself to the main task queue. No allocation — the same task struct re-enters the queue with updated state.</li>\n          <li>If no value is waiting: it adds itself to the upstream task's waiting list, to be re-added when the next input arrives.</li>\n        </ol>\n        <p>Input values are processed one-at-a-time in arrival order. Ten queued inputs means the iterator task visits the queue ten times, advancing the counter and firing a different output path each time.</p>\n\n        <h2 id=\"blocking\">Blocking semantics for long-running operations</h2>\n        <p>The pool's parallelism comes from running N worker threads concurrently on N cores. Each worker is sitting inside a single dispatch task at any given moment. If a box function does something that takes a long time — <code>sleep</code>, blocking I/O, a synchronous network request, waiting on a long-running subprocess — <strong>the worker thread is occupied for the full duration</strong>. It cannot pick up other tasks while it waits.</p>\n\n        <div data-demo=\"threadPool\"></div>\n\n        <p>Concretely:</p>\n        <ul>\n          <li>16-worker pool, 1 box sleeping 10 seconds → the other 15 workers continue normally.</li>\n          <li>16-worker pool, 16 boxes all sleeping → all workers parked, no other task runs until a sleep finishes.</li>\n          <li>The pool size is also the budget for &ldquo;blocking activities&rdquo;. Heavy use of <code>sleep</code>-style boxes means raising <code>SORAMECH_WORKERS</code>.</li>\n        </ul>\n\n        <p><strong>Why the runtime does not have a scheduler:</strong> SoraMech is deliberately not in the business of &ldquo;park this task and wake it at time T.&rdquo; There is no delayed-spawn primitive, no timer thread, no polling loop. Adding one would mean a second concurrency model alongside the pool, with its own synchronization story. Instead, we lean on the pool's existing mechanism: a task either runs (occupying a worker) or is blocked on a slot waiting for a value (parked, no worker held). Long sleeps are an &ldquo;occupying a worker&rdquo; case.</p>\n\n        <div class=\"callout\">\n          <strong>Cooperative pattern. </strong>For users who need many concurrent waits without burning workers, split the operation into &ldquo;kick off the thing&rdquo; (returns immediately) and &ldquo;check whether the thing is done&rdquo; (returns immediately, returns a status), and wire them through an iterator with a queued input. The iterator polls. Each box completes quickly, freeing its worker.\n        </div>\n\n        <h2 id=\"ipc\">The three IPC options</h2>\n\n        <div data-demo=\"ipcOptions\"></div>\n\n        <h3 id=\"ffi\">Option 1 — LuaJIT FFI (Lua ↔ C, in-process)</h3>\n        <p>The Foreign Function Interface lets Lua call C functions that live in a shared library (<code>.so</code>) directly, in the same process, with no subprocess and no channel. You provide a C declaration (<code>ffi.cdef[[ int add(int a, int b); ]]</code>), load the compiled library (<code>ffi.load(\"./mybox.so\")</code>), and call <code>lib.add(3, 4)</code> — the CPU jumps into native code and returns. The box function signature changes from <code>main(argc, argv)</code> to a named function with typed arguments — which is strictly cleaner.</p>\n        <p><strong>Limitation:</strong> FFI only works for languages that compile to a C-compatible ABI. Bash cannot. Python can (via <code>ctypes</code> on the other side), but it's awkward. FFI is the right answer for Lua ↔ C only.</p>\n        <p><strong>Cross-platform:</strong> LuaJIT FFI works on Linux, macOS, and Windows. <code>.so</code> becomes <code>.dylib</code> on macOS and <code>.dll</code> on Windows.</p>\n\n        <h3 id=\"shm\">Option 2 — Shared memory (shm_open + mmap)</h3>\n        <p><code>shm_open(\"/soramech-wire-0\", ...)</code> creates a named memory segment managed by the kernel — not a file on disk, but a named object in RAM. <code>mmap()</code> maps it into the calling process's address space. Any other process that opens the same name gets access to the <em>same physical memory</em>. A write in one process is immediately visible in another — no copy, no syscall per access after setup.</p>\n        <p>For SoraMech, each wire between two boxes would correspond to a named shared memory slot. The compiler generates the slot names and the read/write calls. Any language that can call POSIX can participate:</p>\n        <ul>\n          <li>Lua: via LuaJIT FFI calling <code>shm_open</code> + <code>mmap</code> from libc</li>\n          <li>C: natively</li>\n          <li>Bash: via <code>/dev/shm/&lt;name&gt;</code> — on Linux, the tmpfs backing shared memory is exposed as a filesystem path, so bash can <code>cat /dev/shm/soramech-wire-0</code></li>\n        </ul>\n        <p><strong>Performance:</strong> After the initial <code>mmap()</code> setup, reads and writes are pointer dereferences — no syscalls, no copies.</p>\n        <p><strong>Complication:</strong> Shared memory is untyped raw bytes. You need a size header, a type tag, and a synchronization mechanism. None of these are hard but the compiler must generate all of it correctly for every wire.</p>\n        <p><strong>Cross-platform:</strong> Linux full; macOS partial (<code>shm_open</code> works, <code>/dev/shm/</code> doesn't); Windows different API.</p>\n\n        <h3 id=\"usock\">Option 3 — Unix domain socket servers <span class=\"amber\">(chosen)</span></h3>\n        <p>A Unix domain socket is a socket addressed by a filesystem path instead of an IP address and port. <code>/tmp/soramech-bash.sock</code> is a special file; any process on the same machine connects to it with the standard socket API. The kernel routes data directly between processes in memory — no network stack, no loopback, no protocol headers. Performance is bounded by memory bandwidth.</p>\n        <p>Each language runtime runs as a persistent socket server. One server instance per language per worker thread:</p>\n<pre data-lang=\"paths\">/tmp/soramech-bash-0.sock   ← worker thread 0's bash runtime\n/tmp/soramech-bash-1.sock   ← worker thread 1's bash runtime\n/tmp/soramech-c-0.sock      ← worker thread 0's C runtime</pre>\n        <p><strong>Wire protocol:</strong> Length-prefix framing. The sender writes a 4-byte big-endian integer (the message length in bytes), then that many bytes of content. The receiver reads 4 bytes, then reads exactly that many bytes. This handles values containing newlines or null bytes without ambiguity.</p>\n        <p><strong>Cost of idle servers:</strong> An idle server process is blocked on <code>accept()</code> — zero CPU, approximately 3–5 MB RSS for a bash process. For 10 languages × 4 threads = 40 processes ≈ 150–200 MB. Acceptable.</p>\n        <p><strong>Integration with the SoraMech thread pool:</strong></p>\n        <p>Each worker thread owns its set of language server sockets. When <code>run_task</code> calls a cross-language box, it sends to the socket and blocks on the read — the thread blocks, not the whole program. Other workers continue processing other boxes on other cores. The server processes run concurrently on whatever cores the OS schedules them to. This gives real parallelism: a bash box and a C box assigned to different workers can run simultaneously.</p>\n        <p><strong>Cross-platform:</strong> Linux full; macOS full; Windows 10 1803+ (2018) supported.</p>\n\n        <h2 id=\"summary\">Summary comparison</h2>\n        <table>\n          <thead><tr><th>Property</th><th>FFI (.so)</th><th>Shared memory</th><th>Unix domain socket</th></tr></thead>\n          <tbody>\n            <tr><td>Speed (per call)</td>      <td>nanoseconds</td>    <td>nanoseconds*</td>      <td>microseconds</td></tr>\n            <tr><td>Languages supported</td>   <td>C-ABI only</td>     <td>any (with caveats)</td><td>any</td></tr>\n            <tr><td>Parallel connections</td>  <td>N/A (in-process)</td><td>yes (with sync)</td>  <td>yes (natural)</td></tr>\n            <tr><td>Linux</td>                 <td>yes</td>            <td>yes</td>               <td>yes</td></tr>\n            <tr><td>macOS</td>                 <td>yes</td>            <td>partial†</td>          <td>yes</td></tr>\n            <tr><td>Windows</td>               <td>yes (.dll)</td>     <td>no (different API)</td><td>yes (Win10+)</td></tr>\n            <tr><td>Complexity</td>            <td>low</td>            <td>medium</td>            <td>low-medium</td></tr>\n          </tbody>\n        </table>\n        <p class=\"tiny dim\">*After initial mmap setup. †shm_open works; /dev/shm filesystem path does not.</p>\n\n        <p>The compiler (issue 219, folded into issue 309) uses FFI for Lua ↔ C wires where the C source is compiled to a <code>.so</code>, and Unix domain sockets for all other cross-language wires. Done. The HTML notebook lives at `docs/HTML/` and the markdown TOC now points to it.

**What's there:**

```
docs/HTML/
  index.html                  ← TOC landing with animated dataflow
  001-architecture.html       ← 5 interactive demos
  002-roadmap.html            ← timeline cards
  003-driver-system.html      ← driver-vs-spec animation
  004-ipc-and-threading.html  ← thread-pool & IPC comparison
  005-language-specs.html     ← lang_spec_t explorer, live lexer
  assets/style.css            ← design system
  assets/nav.js               ← sidebar + scroll-spy
  assets/demos.js             ← all 13 interactive demos
```

**Aesthetic.** Engineering notebook lit by an amber desk lamp. Warm near-black background with a soft radial glow, sepia cream text, lamp-amber and oxidized-copper accents, very subtle paper-grain overlay. Type: **Fraunces** (variable serif with optical sizes — including italic display + light-weight headlines), **JetBrains Mono** for code, **Caveat** for handwritten marginalia ("strings flow like ink ↗" etc.). Demo frames have a tick-mark top edge like surveyor's tape.

**Sidebar.** Persistent on every page. Brand mark, doc list with section numbers (§00–§05), and a scroll-spy sub-nav that auto-builds from the current page's `<h2>` elements and highlights as you scroll. Built once in `nav.js` so every page is consistent.

**13 interactive demos.**
- **Architecture page**: three-program diagram with hover-highlight wires; routing-kinds explorer (pick plain/comparator/iterator/weighted/distributor, fire the box, watch the right branch light up with an animated pulse); weighted-slider inspector with live histogram of 1000 simulated runs; slot-store push/pop visualizer with mode toggle (1-cell peek vs N-cell ring); cell-tagging side-by-side (FIFO vs tag-order pop after out-of-order pushes); iterator counter with spawn/run/reset and rotating branch firing.
- **Roadmap**: timeline cards with status pills, progress bars, hover-glow.
- **Driver system**: animated comparison of phase-2 shell-out (with a slow dot moving 2s, "process spawn" ghosts) vs phase-3 spec direct call (0.15s, `dlsym → call` annotation), with toggle.
- **IPC & Threading**: log-scaled bar chart comparing FFI / shm / Unix socket / driver latency; click-to-cycle worker pool (idle → working → blocked) with live capacity readout.
- **Language specs**: clickable `lang_spec_t` callbacks showing when each runs; live Lua tokenizer (edit text in the textarea, watch tokens recolour with a tally).

Open it locally with:

```
cd /mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech && python3 -m http.server 8765 --bind 127.0.0.1
```

then visit `http://127.0.0.1:8765/docs/HTML/`. (Or just `xdg-open docs/HTML/index.html` — only the Google Fonts import needs network, everything else works offline.)

7. **304 — dispatch layer**. The plumbing that ties everything together.
8. **310, 307, 308, 311, 312** thereafter.

{
  "content":"/* src/009-slot-store.h — per-input-port slot store, public API.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: a thread-safe pool of ring-buffer\n * slots, allocated at graph load time, used by the phase 3\n * dispatch layer to route values between boxes.\n *\n * Slots belong to input ports, not tasks. Each box has one slot\n * per input port; the slot persists for the whole run. A wire is\n * a routing declaration — when a producer's task finishes, the\n * dispatch layer pushes copies of the output into every\n * downstream input slot. Fan-out is N pushes; fan-in is N\n * producers pushing into one slot. Designed in issue 302.\n *\n * Three slot modes, chosen via flags at slot_alloc:\n *\n *   1-cell peek (n_cells == 1, no flags)\n *     — for literals and wires from producers that run exactly\n *       once. Push once at startup. Every consumer task peeks\n *       without draining; the cell stays filled.\n *\n *   N-cell pop (n_cells > 1, no flags)\n *     — for wires whose producer runs many times (iterators,\n *       queued inputs). Push appends to tail; pop drains head\n *       FIFO. Consumer task pops one cell per spawn.\n *\n *   N-cell pop, tagged (SLOT_TAGGED)\n *     — same shape as N-cell pop, but pop returns the cell with\n *       the lowest tag, not the head. Used downstream of parallel\n *       iterators where push order is non-deterministic but\n *       consumption order must follow the iterator counter.\n *\n *   atomic counter (SLOT_ATOMIC_COUNTER, n_cells and cell_capacity\n *     ignored)\n *     — single atomic uint32. Read-and-increment via\n *       slot_read_inc(). Used for iterator / randomizer /\n *       weighted-routing counters. Concurrent reads each get a\n *       distinct value mod the caller-supplied bound.\n *\n * Synchronization is per-slot. There is no allocator-wide lock on\n * the hot read/write path. The atomic-counter slot uses\n * atomic_fetch_add; the ring-buffer slots use a per-slot spinlock\n * around header mutation (one byte, atomic_flag).\n *\n * Lifetime is the run. Slots are freed when the store is\n * destroyed at the end of the run — there is no per-slot refcount\n * and no end-of-stream propagation. Run termination is governed\n * by the pool's active-task counter (issue 301).\n *\n * Errors: a return of -1 from a read/write op means the operation\n * could not be performed (empty pop, buffer too small, type\n * mismatch). The store does not assert or abort; the dispatch\n * layer is expected to check return codes. The hard-crash policy\n * applies at the language-spec layer, not here.\n *\n * What's NOT in this version:\n *  - Size-class free lists and coalescing. The design in issue 302\n *    describes a segregated allocator with eager-coalesce; this\n *    initial implementation uses plain malloc per slot. The pattern\n *    is \"allocate once at graph load, free at run end\", so free-list\n *    optimization buys nothing for the current usage. Lands as a\n *    follow-on if profiling justifies it.\n *  - Large-value heap for variable-size payloads. Slots store\n *    fixed-size cells; very large outputs (LLM responses) will\n *    use a separate two-tier scheme. Follow-on within 302.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_SLOT_STORE_H\n#define SORAMECH_SLOT_STORE_H\n\n#include <stdint.h>\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n/* {{{ Types & flags */\ntypedef struct slot_store slot_store_t;\ntypedef int32_t           slot_id_t;\n\n#define SLOT_INVALID  ((slot_id_t)-1)\n\n/* slot_alloc flags */\nenum {\n    SLOT_FLAG_NONE           = 0,\n    SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED         = 1 << 0,\n    SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER = 1 << 1,\n};\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Store lifecycle */\n/* Construct an empty store. Returns NULL on allocation failure. */\nslot_store_t *slot_store_create(void);\n\n/* Free every slot and the store itself. Safe to call on NULL. */\nvoid          slot_store_destroy(slot_store_t *s);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Slot lifecycle */\n/* Allocate a slot.\n *\n *   cell_capacity — bytes per cell. Ignored for SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER.\n *   n_cells       — ring size (1 for peek slots, >1 for pop). Ignored for\n *                   SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER.\n *   flags         — zero, SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED, or SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER.\n *\n * Returns the new slot's id, or SLOT_INVALID on allocation failure or\n * invalid arguments. Ids are stable for the lifetime of the store. */\nslot_id_t     slot_alloc(slot_store_t *s,\n                         int32_t cell_capacity,\n                         int32_t n_cells,\n                         int32_t flags);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Ring-buffer ops */\n/* Push a value into the slot's next free cell.\n *\n *   data, size — value bytes. size must be <= cell_capacity.\n *   tag        — ordering tag. Carried only on SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED slots;\n *                ignored otherwise.\n *\n * Returns 0 on success, -1 if the slot is full or arguments invalid.\n * Not valid on SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER slots (returns -1). */\nint           slot_push(slot_store_t *s, slot_id_t id,\n                        const void *data, int32_t size, uint32_t tag);\n\n/* Peek at the head cell without draining it.\n *\n *   buf, buf_size — destination. {
  "content":"# 009-slot-store.c — public surface\n\nPer-input-port slot store. Allocated once at graph load; each box\ninput port owns one slot, freed when the run ends. The dispatch\nlayer reads and writes through this API; language specs never see\nslot IDs (issue 303 keeps that boundary clean).\n\n## Lifecycle\n\n- `slot_store_t *slot_store_create(void)` — empty store; NULL on OOM.\n- `void slot_store_destroy(slot_store_t *s)` — frees every slot.\n\n## Allocation\n\n- `slot_id_t slot_alloc(store, cell_capacity, n_cells, flags)`\n  - Returns `SLOT_INVALID` on bad args / OOM.\n  - Flags: `SLOT_FLAG_NONE`, `SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED`, `SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER`.\n  - `cell_capacity` and `n_cells` are ignored for atomic-counter slots.\n\n## Ring-buffer ops (push / peek / pop / has_value / fill_count)\n\n- `int slot_push(store, id, data, size, tag)` — 0 on success, -1 on\n  full / wrong type / size too big.\n- `int32_t slot_peek(store, id, buf, buf_size)` — returns the cell's\n  filled_size on success; -1 on empty / wrong type / buf too small.\n  Does not advance head. Used for 1-cell peek slots.\n- `int32_t slot_pop(store, id, buf, buf_size)` — drains. Untagged\n  pops head FIFO; tagged pops the lowest-tag filled cell.\n- `int slot_has_value(store, id)` — 1 if a value is available.\n- `int32_t slot_fill_count(store, id)` — number of filled cells.\n\n## Atomic-counter slot\n\n- `uint32_t slot_read_inc(store, id, mod)` — fetch-and-add. Returns\n  the pre-increment counter value mod the supplied bound.\n  `UINT32_MAX` on wrong type or `mod == 0`.\n\n## Thread safety\n\n- The atomic-counter slot uses `atomic_fetch_add_explicit`; no lock.\n- Ring-buffer slots use a per-slot `atomic_flag` spinlock around\n  header + cell mutations.\n- The store itself is single-threaded for allocation (graph-load\n  phase); after that, the slot array is read-only and per-slot\n  operations run concurrently.\n\n## What's NOT here (deferred)\n\n- Size-class free lists / coalescing — plain `malloc` per slot for\n  now. The current usage pattern doesn't reuse slot memory, so\n  optimization buys nothing yet.\n- Large-value heap for variable-size payloads. Follow-on within\n  issue 302.\n\n## Related\n\n- Issue 302 — design.\n- Issue 304 — the dispatch layer that calls this API.\n- Issue 301 — the pool whose workers contend on these slots.\n",

}

memset(buf, 0, 2); ASSERT(slot_pop(s, id, buf, 2) == 1); ASSERT(buf[0] == 'C');\n    memset(buf, 0, 2); ASSERT(slot_pop(s, id, buf, 2) == 1); ASSERT(buf[0] == 'D');\n    ASSERT(slot_pop(s, id, buf, 2) = 8, N_READS = 1000 };\n    slot_store_t *s = slot_store_create();\n    slot_id_t id = slot_alloc(s, 0, 0, SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER);\n\n    pthread_t   threads[N_THREADS];\n    uint32_t    out[N_THREADS * N_READS];\n    struct counter_args args[N_THREADS];\n\n    for (int t = 0; t < N_THREADS; t++) {\n        args[t].store = s;\n        args[t].id    = id;\n        args[t].n     = N_READS;\n        args[t].out   = out + t * N_READS;\n        pthread_create(&threads[t], NULL, counter_worker, &args[t]);\n    }\n    for (int t = 0; t < N_THREADS; t++) pthread_join(threads[t], NULL);\n\n    /* Every value must be unique and cover 0..N_THREADS*N_READS-1. */\n    qsort(out, N_THREADS * N_READS, sizeof out[0], cmp_u32);\n    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < N_THREADS * N_READS; i++) {\n        ASSERT(out[i] == i);\n    }\n    slot_store_destroy(s);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Concurrent push/pop on an N-cell ring */\nstruct prod_args {\n    slot_store_t *store;\n    slot_id_t     id;\n    int           n;\n};\n\nstatic void *producer(void *arg)\n{\n    struct prod_args *a = arg;\n    for (int i = 0; i < a->n; i++) {\n        /* Spin if ring full; producer/consumer race intentionally. */\n        while (slot_push(a->store, a->id, &i, (int)sizeof i, 0) != 0) {\n            /* busy-wait */\n        }\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nstatic void *consumer(void *arg)\n{\n    struct prod_args *a = arg;\n    int seen = 0;\n    int sum  = 0;\n    while (seen < a->n) {\n        int v;\n        if (slot_pop(a->store, a->id, &v, (int)sizeof v) > 0) {\n            sum += v;\n            seen++;\n        }\n    }\n    *(int *)arg = sum;   /* abuse: write sum back through arg.n field */\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nstatic int test_concurrent_push_pop(void)\n{\n    enum { N = 5000 };\n    slot_store_t *s = slot_store_create();\n    slot_id_t id = slot_alloc(s, (int)sizeof(int), 16, SLOT_FLAG_NONE);\n\n    struct prod_args pa = { s, id, N };\n    struct prod_args ca = { s, id, N };\n    pthread_t tp, tc;\n    pthread_create(&tp, NULL, producer, &pa);\n    pthread_create(&tc, NULL, consumer, &ca);\n    pthread_join(tp, NULL);\n    pthread_join(tc, NULL);\n\n    /* Consumer summed every value it read.   "old_string":"/* {{{ Concurrent push/pop on an N-cell ring */\nstruct prod_args {\n    slot_store_t *store;\n    slot_id_t     id;\n    int           n;\n};\n\nstatic void *producer(void *arg)\n{\n    struct prod_args *a = arg;\n    for (int i = 0; i < a->n; i++) {\n        /* Spin if ring full; producer/consumer race intentionally. */\n        while (slot_push(a->store, a->id, &i, (int)sizeof i, 0) != 0) {\n            /* busy-wait */\n        }\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nstatic void *consumer(void *arg)\n{\n    struct prod_args *a = arg;\n    int seen = 0;\n    int sum  = 0;\n    while (seen < a->n) {\n        int v;\n        if (slot_pop(a->store, a->id, &v, (int)sizeof v) > 0) {\n            sum += v;\n            seen++;\n        }\n    }\n    *(int *)arg = sum;   /* abuse: write sum back through arg.n field */\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nstatic int test_concurrent_push_pop(void)\n{\n    enum { N = 5000 };\n    slot_store_t *s = slot_store_create();\n    slot_id_t id = slot_alloc(s, (int)sizeof(int), 16, SLOT_FLAG_NONE);\n\n    struct prod_args pa = { s, id, N };\n    struct prod_args ca = { s, id, N };\n    pthread_t tp, tc;\n    pthread_create(&tp, NULL, producer, &pa);\n    pthread_create(&tc, NULL, consumer, &ca);\n    pthread_join(tp, NULL);\n    pthread_join(tc, NULL);\n\n    /* Consumer summed every value it read. The producer pushed\n     * 0..N-1, so the expected total is N*(N-1)/2. The \"sum\" was\n     * stashed into ca.n (yes, ugly). */\n    int expected = N * (N - 1) / 2;\n    ASSERT(ca.n == expected);\n\n    slot_store_destroy(s);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */"
}

Three pieces land together\nsince they're meaningless apart: there's a Makefile to build with,\nthe first real piece of runtime code (the slot store), and the\nworking directory swept clean of the user content that was\naccidentally tracked.\n\nThe build orchestration grows a top-level Makefile that turns the\nrunner sources into a single binary and each language directory\ninto its own shared library. Three modes — release by default,\ndebug with symbols, and a strict mode that promotes warnings to\nerrors — share the same source discovery: a glob over the source\ntree picks up new files automatically as future issues land them.\nThe runner is currently a single-file stub that parses argv,\nprints what it would do, and exits, and each of the three reference\nlanguage stubs exports the expected symbol with NULL callbacks —\njust enough that the spec registry can dlopen and inspect them once\nthat lands. A small editor config matches the include paths so\nLSP integrations resolve the same way the compiler does.\n\nThe slot store is the first real runtime component. It owns three\nshapes of slot behind one API: a one-cell peek mode for literals\nand run-once wires, an N-cell pop ring for queued and multi-push\nwires, and an atomic-counter mode that backs iterator and weighted\nrouting. The pop ring optionally honours an ordering tag — a push\ncarries the producer's counter snapshot, and pop returns the\nlowest-tag filled cell, preserving iteration order under parallel\niterator workers. Concurrency is per-slot: a one-byte spinlock\nguards header and cell mutations on the ring slots, while the\natomic counter goes straight through fetch-and-add with no lock.\n\nTwelve unit tests exercise every read mode, the buffer-too-small\nand ring-full edge cases, the bad-id path, the tagged ordering\nguarantee, and two threaded races — eight threads pulling a\nmillion-value-range counter and a producer/consumer pair shuffling\nfive thousand integers through a sixteen-cell ring. All pass under\nstrict-mode warnings-as-errors.\n\nTwo pieces of the slot store design are deferred to follow-ons:\nthe size-class free list with coalescing, and the large-value\nheap that backs variable-size payloads. Neither blocks 301 / 304 /\n305 / 306 / 307 / 308; the first is a pure optimization and the\nsecond only matters once a graph wants outputs whose size isn't\nknown at compile time.\n\nMaps stop being tracked as well. The user content that had\naccumulated under maps/* gets removed from the index; the working\ntree is untouched, and the blanket gitignore from the previous\ncommit keeps future contents out.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\"\necho \"---\"\ngit log --oneline -5",
  "description":"Commit phase 3 foundation"
}

{
  "content":"/* libs/json/json.c — DOM JSON parser + streaming writer.\n *\n * Sections, top to bottom:\n *\n *   - Arena allocator (chunked bump).\n *   - Internal node types and tagged-union layout.\n *   - Parser (hand-rolled recursive descent).\n *   - Accessors.\n *   - File loader (json_parse_file).\n *   - Writer (declared; body deferred per the implementation log on\n *     issue 314 — JSONL writer lands when 311 needs it).\n *\n * Designed in issue 314. The parser supports JSON per RFC 8259 with\n * a few tightenings: no comments, no trailing commas, no embedded\n * NULs in strings, BMP-only \\uXXXX with surrogate-pair handling.\n * Numbers are doubles; integer-shaped fields are read via\n * (int)json_number_value.\n *\n * Memory model: every node and every string lives in the arena\n * passed to json_parse. json_arena_destroy frees the lot in one\n * call. There is no per-node free. During parsing, temporary\n * linked-list scaffolding for array/object construction is also\n * allocated in the arena and left \"abandoned\" once the final\n * fixed-size arrays are emitted — abandoned bytes are reclaimed\n * when the arena is destroyed.\n */\n\n#include \"json.h\"\n\n#include <stdint.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ Arena allocator */\ntypedef struct json_chunk {\n    struct json_chunk *next;\n    size_t size;\n    size_t used;\n    /* Followed by `size` bytes of storage. */\n    char data[];\n} json_chunk_t;\n\nstruct json_arena {\n    json_chunk_t *head;\n    size_t total_bytes;\n};\n\n#define JSON_CHUNK_DEFAULT 16384\n\n/* {{{ arena_new_chunk() */\nstatic json_chunk_t *arena_new_chunk(size_t min_size)\n{\n    size_t sz = (min_size > JSON_CHUNK_DEFAULT) ? min_size : JSON_CHUNK_DEFAULT;\n    json_chunk_t *c = malloc(sizeof(json_chunk_t) + sz);\n    if (!c) return NULL;\n    c->next = NULL;\n    c->size = sz;\n    c->used = 0;\n    return c;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ json_arena_create() */\njson_arena_t *json_arena_create(void)\n{\n    json_arena_t *a = calloc(1, sizeof *a);\n    if (!a) return NULL;\n    a->head = arena_new_chunk(JSON_CHUNK_DEFAULT);\n    if (!a->head) { free(a); return NULL; }\n    a->total_bytes = a->head->size;\n    return a;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ json_arena_destroy() */\nvoid json_arena_destroy(json_arena_t *a)\n{\n    if (!a) return;\n    json_chunk_t *c = a->head;\n    while (c) {\n        json_chunk_t *next = c->next;\n        free(c);\n        c = next;\n    }\n    free(a);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ json_arena_bytes() */\nsize_t json_arena_bytes(const json_arena_t *a)\n{\n    return a ? a->total_bytes : 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ arena_alloc() — aligned to 8 bytes */\nstatic void *arena_alloc(json_arena_t *a, size_t bytes)\n{\n    if (bytes == 0) bytes = 1;\n    /* 8-byte alignment for everything; the union contains a double\n     * and pointers, both of which want at least 8-byte alignment on\n     * 64-bit targets. */\n    size_t aligned = (bytes + 7u) & ~(size_t)7u;\n\n    if (a->head->used + aligned > a->head->size) {\n        json_chunk_t *c = arena_new_chunk(aligned);\n        if (!c) return NULL;\n        c->next = a->head;\n        a->head = c;\n        a->total_bytes += c->size;\n    }\n    void *p = a->head->data + a->head->used;\n    a->head->used += aligned;\n    return p;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ arena_strdup() — copy a length-counted byte run, NUL-terminate */\nstatic char *arena_strdup(json_arena_t *a, const char *s, size_t len)\n{\n    char *out = arena_alloc(a, len + 1);\n    if (!out) return NULL;\n    if (len > 0) memcpy(out, s, len);\n    out[len] = '\\0';\n    return out;\n}\n/* }}} */\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Node layout */\ntypedef struct kv_link {\n    struct kv_link *next;\n    const char     *key;     /* arena-allocated; NULL for array items */\n    json_node_t    *value;\n} kv_link_t;\n\nstruct json_node {\n    json_kind_t kind;\n    union {\n        int           b;\n        double        n;\n        const char   *s;\n        struct {\n            json_node_t **items;\n            int           count;\n        } arr;\n        struct {\n            const char  **keys;\n            json_node_t **values;\n            int           count;\n        } obj;\n    } u;\n};\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Parser state */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char  *src;\n    int          pos;     /* current byte offset into src */\n    json_arena_t *arena;\n    const char  *err_msg; /* set on first failure */\n    int          err_pos;\n} parser_t;\n\nstatic json_node_t *parse_value(parser_t *p);\nstatic int          parse_string_into(parser_t *p, const char **out);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helpers — error reporting & character classes */\nstatic void fail(parser_t *p, const char *msg)\n{\n    if (!p->err_msg) {\n        p->err_msg = msg;\n        p->err_pos = p->pos;\n    }\n}\n\nstatic int is_ws(int c)   { return c == ' ' || c == '\\t' || c == '\\n' || c == '\\r'; }\nstatic int is_digit(int c){ return c >= '0' && c <= '9'; }\nstatic int is_hex(int c)\n{\n    return (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || (c >= 'a' && c <= 'f') || (c >= 'A' && c <= 'F');\n}\n\nstatic int hex_val(int c)\n{\n    if (c >= '0' && c <= '9') return c - '0';\n    if (c >= 'a' && c <= 'f') return c - 'a' + 10;\n    if (c >= 'A' && c <= 'F') return c - 'A' + 10;\n    return 0;\n}\n\nstatic int peek(parser_t *p)\n{\n    return (unsigned char)p->src[p->pos];\n}\n\nstatic void skip_ws(parser_t *p)\n{\n    while (is_ws((unsigned char)p->src[p->pos])) p->pos++;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helpers — node makers */\nstatic json_node_t *mk_node(parser_t *p, json_kind_t k)\n{\n    json_node_t *n = arena_alloc(p->arena, sizeof *n);\n    if (!n) { fail(p, \"out of memory\"); return NULL; }\n    memset(n, 0, sizeof *n);\n    n->kind = k;\n    return n;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ parse_string_into() — read \"...\", decode escapes into arena */\n/* Reads from the opening '\"' at p->pos. On success advances p past\n * the closing '\"' and sets *out to an arena-owned NUL-terminated\n * UTF-8 string. */\nstatic int parse_string_into(parser_t *p, const char **out)\n{\n    if (peek(p) != '\"') { fail(p, \"expected string\"); return 0; }\n    p->pos++;\n\n    /* First pass: scan to closing quote, count decoded bytes. */\n    int start = p->pos;\n    int decoded_len = 0;\n    while (1) {\n        int c = peek(p);\n        if (c == 0) { fail(p, \"unterminated string\"); return 0; }\n        if (c == '\"') break;\n        if (c == '\\\\') {\n            p->pos++;\n            int e = peek(p);\n            switch (e) {\n                case '\"': case '\\\\': case '/':\n                case 'b': case 'f': case 'n': case 'r': case 't':\n                    decoded_len += 1; p->pos++; break;\n                case 'u': {\n                    /* 4 hex digits → 1..4 UTF-8 bytes; surrogate pairs\n                     * combine to 4 bytes. We compute conservatively\n                     * during the count pass. */\n                    p->pos++;\n                    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {\n                        if (!is_hex(peek(p))) { fail(p, \"bad \\\\u escape\"); return 0; }\n                        p->pos++;\n                    }\n                    /* Possible surrogate pair? If high surrogate, consume\n                     * the second \\uXXXX too. */\n                    /* We can't know the codepoint without decoding, so\n                     * we add the worst case (4) and refine in pass 2. */\n                    decoded_len += 4;\n                    break;\n                }\n                default: fail(p, \"invalid escape sequence\"); return 0;\n            }\n        } else if ((unsigned)c < 0x20) {\n            fail(p, \"unescaped control character in string\");\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            decoded_len++;\n            p->pos++;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /* Second pass: actually decode. */\n    int end = p->pos;\n    char *buf = arena_alloc(p->arena, (size_t)decoded_len + 1);\n    if (!buf) { fail(p, \"out of memory\"); return 0; }\n    int o = 0;\n    p->pos = start;\n    while (p->pos < end) {\n        int c = peek(p);\n        if (c == '\\\\') {\n            p->pos++;\n            int e = peek(p);\n            p->pos++;\n            switch (e) {\n                case '\"':  buf[o++] = '\"';  break;\n                case '\\\\': buf[o++] = '\\\\'; break;\n                case '/':  buf[o++] = '/';  break;\n                case 'b':  buf[o++] = '\\b'; break;\n                case 'f':  buf[o++] = '\\f'; break;\n                case 'n':  buf[o++] = '\\n'; break;\n                case 'r':  buf[o++] = '\\r'; break;\n                case 't':  buf[o++] = '\\t'; break;\n                case 'u': {\n                    int cp = 0;\n                    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {\n                        cp = (cp << 4) | hex_val(peek(p));\n                        p->pos++;\n                    }\n                    /* High surrogate? */\n                    if (cp >= 0xD800 && cp <= 0xDBFF) {\n                        if (p->src[p->pos] != '\\\\' || p->src[p->pos + 1] != 'u') {\n                            fail(p, \"lone high surrogate\");\n                            return 0;\n                        }\n                        p->pos += 2;\n                        int cp2 = 0;\n                        for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {\n                            if (!is_hex(peek(p))) { fail(p, \"bad \\\\u escape\"); return 0; }\n                            cp2 = (cp2 << 4) | hex_val(peek(p));\n                            p->pos++;\n                        }\n                        if (cp2 < 0xDC00 || cp2 > 0xDFFF) {\n                            fail(p, \"expected low surrogate\");\n                            return 0;\n                        }\n                        cp = 0x10000 + (((cp - 0xD800) << 10) | (cp2 - 0xDC00));\n                    } else if (cp >= 0xDC00 && cp <= 0xDFFF) {\n                        fail(p, \"lone low surrogate\");\n                        return 0;\n                    }\n                    if (cp == 0) {\n                        fail(p, \"embedded NUL not allowed\");\n                        return 0;\n                    }\n                    /* Encode UTF-8. */\n                    if (cp < 0x80) {\n                        buf[o++] = (char)cp;\n                    } else if (cp < 0x800) {\n                        buf[o++] = (char)(0xC0 | (cp >> 6));\n                        buf[o++] = (char)(0x80 | (cp & 0x3F));\n                    } else if (cp < 0x10000) {\n                        buf[o++] = (char)(0xE0 | (cp >> 12));\n                        buf[o++] = (char)(0x80 | ((cp >> 6) & 0x3F));\n                        buf[o++] = (char)(0x80 | (cp & 0x3F));\n                    } else {\n                        buf[o++] = (char)(0xF0 | (cp >> 18));\n                        buf[o++] = (char)(0x80 | ((cp >> 12) & 0x3F));\n                        buf[o++] = (char)(0x80 | ((cp >> 6) & 0x3F));\n                        buf[o++] = (char)(0x80 | (cp & 0x3F));\n                    }\n                    break;\n                }\n                default: /* impossible — pass 1 caught it */ break;\n            }\n        } else {\n            buf[o++] = (char)c;\n            p->pos++;\n        }\n    }\n    buf[o] = '\\0';\n    p->pos++;  /* past the closing '\"' */\n    *out = buf;\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ parse_number() */\nstatic json_node_t *parse_number(parser_t *p)\n{\n    int start = p->pos;\n    if (peek(p) == '-') p->pos++;\n    if (!is_digit(peek(p))) { fail(p, \"invalid number\"); return NULL; }\n    if (peek(p) == '0') {\n        p->pos++;\n    } else {\n        while (is_digit(peek(p))) p->pos++;\n    }\n    if (peek(p) == '.') {\n        p->pos++;\n        if (!is_digit(peek(p))) { fail(p, \"expected digit after '.'\"); return NULL; }\n        while (is_digit(peek(p))) p->pos++;\n    }\n    if (peek(p) == 'e' || peek(p) == 'E') {\n        p->pos++;\n        if (peek(p) == '+' || peek(p) == '-') p->pos++;\n        if (!is_digit(peek(p))) { fail(p, \"expected digit in exponent\"); return NULL; }\n        while (is_digit(peek(p))) p->pos++;\n    }\n\n    int len = p->pos - start;\n    /* Copy into a scratch NUL-terminated buffer for strtod. 64 bytes\n     * covers any double-representable literal. Longer literals get a\n     * heap fallback. */\n    char small[64];\n    char *buf = small;\n    char *heap = NULL;\n    if (len >= (int)sizeof small) {\n        heap = malloc((size_t)len + 1);\n        if (!heap) { fail(p, \"out of memory\"); return NULL; }\n        buf = heap;\n    }\n    memcpy(buf, p->src + start, (size_t)len);\n    buf[len] = '\\0';\n\n    char *endp;\n    double v = strtod(buf, &endp);\n    if (endp != buf + len) {\n        if (heap) free(heap);\n        fail(p, \"invalid number\");\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    if (heap) free(heap);\n\n    json_node_t *n = mk_node(p, JSON_NUMBER);\n    if (!n) return NULL;\n    n->u.n = v;\n    return n;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ parse_literal() — true / false / null */\nstatic json_node_t *parse_literal(parser_t *p)\n{\n    const char *s = p->src + p->pos;\n    if (strncmp(s, \"true\", 4) == 0) {\n        p->pos += 4;\n        json_node_t *n = mk_node(p, JSON_BOOL);\n        if (n) n->u.b = 1;\n        return n;\n    }\n    if (strncmp(s, \"false\", 5) == 0) {\n        p->pos += 5;\n        json_node_t *n = mk_node(p, JSON_BOOL);\n        if (n) n->u.b = 0;\n        return n;\n    }\n    if (strncmp(s, \"null\", 4) == 0) {\n        p->pos += 4;\n        return mk_node(p, JSON_NULL);\n    }\n    fail(p, \"unexpected token\");\n    return NULL;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ parse_array() */\nstatic json_node_t *parse_array(parser_t *p)\n{\n    if (peek(p) != '[') { fail(p, \"expected '['\"); return NULL; }\n    p->pos++;\n    skip_ws(p);\n\n    kv_link_t *head = NULL, *tail = NULL;\n    int count = 0;\n\n    if (peek(p) == ']') {\n        p->pos++;\n        json_node_t *n = mk_node(p, JSON_ARRAY);\n        if (n) { n->u.arr.items = NULL; n->u.arr.count = 0; }\n        return n;\n    }\n\n    while (1) {\n        json_node_t *v = parse_value(p);\n        if (!v) return NULL;\n        kv_link_t *link = arena_alloc(p->arena, sizeof *link);\n        if (!link) { fail(p, \"out of memory\"); return NULL; }\n        link->next = NULL;\n        link->key  = NULL;\n        link->value = v;\n        if (!head) head = link;\n        else       tail->next = link;\n        tail = link;\n        count++;\n\n        skip_ws(p);\n        if (peek(p) == ',') {\n            p->pos++;\n            skip_ws(p);\n            if (peek(p) == ']') { fail(p, \"trailing comma\"); return NULL; }\n        } else if (peek(p) == ']') {\n            p->pos++;\n            break;\n        } else {\n            fail(p, \"expected ',' or ']'\");\n            return NULL;\n        }\n    }\n\n    json_node_t *n = mk_node(p, JSON_ARRAY);\n    if (!n) return NULL;\n    n->u.arr.count = count;\n    n->u.arr.items = arena_alloc(p->arena, (size_t)count * sizeof(json_node_t *));\n    if (!n->u.arr.items) { fail(p, \"out of memory\"); return NULL; }\n    int i = 0;\n    for (kv_link_t *l = head; l; l = l->next) n->u.arr.items[i++] = l->value;\n    return n;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ parse_object() */\nstatic json_node_t *parse_object(parser_t *p)\n{\n    if (peek(p) != '{') { fail(p, \"expected '{'\"); return NULL; }\n    p->pos++;\n    skip_ws(p);\n\n    kv_link_t *head = NULL, *tail = NULL;\n    int count = 0;\n\n    if (peek(p) == '}') {\n        p->pos++;\n        json_node_t *n = mk_node(p, JSON_OBJECT);\n        if (n) { n->u.obj.keys = NULL; n->u.obj.values = NULL; n->u.obj.count = 0; }\n        return n;\n    }\n\n    while (1) {\n        skip_ws(p);\n        const char *key;\n        if (!parse_string_into(p, &key)) return NULL;\n        skip_ws(p);\n        if (peek(p) != ':') { fail(p, \"expected ':' after key\"); return NULL; }\n        p->pos++;\n        skip_ws(p);\n        json_node_t *v = parse_value(p);\n        if (!v) return NULL;\n\n        kv_link_t *link = arena_alloc(p->arena, sizeof *link);\n        if (!link) { fail(p, \"out of memory\"); return NULL; }\n        link->next  = NULL;\n        link->key   = key;\n        link->value = v;\n        if (!head) head = link;\n        else       tail->next = link;\n        tail = link;\n        count++;\n\n        skip_ws(p);\n        if (peek(p) == ',') {\n            p->pos++;\n            skip_ws(p);\n            if (peek(p) == '}') { fail(p, \"trailing comma\"); return NULL; }\n        } else if (peek(p) == '}') {\n            p->pos++;\n            break;\n        } else {\n            fail(p, \"expected ',' or '}'\");\n            return NULL;\n        }\n    }\n\n    json_node_t *n = mk_node(p, JSON_OBJECT);\n    if (!n) return NULL;\n    n->u.obj.count  = count;\n    n->u.obj.keys   = arena_alloc(p->arena, (size_t)count * sizeof(const char *));\n    n->u.obj.values = arena_alloc(p->arena, (size_t)count * sizeof(json_node_t *));\n    if (!n->u.obj.keys || !n->u.obj.values) {\n        fail(p, \"out of memory\");\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    int i = 0;\n    for (kv_link_t *l = head; l; l = l->next) {\n        n->u.obj.keys[i]   = l->key;\n        n->u.obj.values[i] = l->value;\n        i++;\n    }\n    return n;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ parse_value() — dispatch on first non-space char */\nstatic json_node_t *parse_value(parser_t *p)\n{\n    skip_ws(p);\n    int c = peek(p);\n    if (c == '{')                                 return parse_object(p);\n    if (c == '[')                                 return parse_array(p);\n    if (c == '\"') {\n        json_node_t *n = mk_node(p, JSON_STRING);\n        if (!n) return NULL;\n        if (!parse_string_into(p, &n->u.s)) return NULL;\n        return n;\n    }\n    if (c == '-' || is_digit(c))                  return parse_number(p);\n    if (c == 't' || c == 'f' || c == 'n')         return parse_literal(p);\n    fail(p, \"unexpected character\");\n    return NULL;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ json_parse() */\njson_node_t *json_parse(json_arena_t *a, const char *src,\n                        int *err_offset, const char **err_msg)\n{\n    parser_t p = { src, 0, a, NULL, 0 };\n    if (!src || !a) {\n        if (err_msg)    *err_msg    = \"null arena or source\";\n        if (err_offset) *err_offset = 0;\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    json_node_t *root = parse_value(&p);\n    if (!root) {\n        if (err_msg)    *err_msg    = p.err_msg ? p.err_msg : \"parse error\";\n        if (err_offset) *err_offset = p.err_pos;\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    skip_ws(&p);\n    if (p.src[p.pos] != '\\0') {\n        if (err_msg)    *err_msg    = \"trailing garbage after JSON value\";\n        if (err_offset) *err_offset = p.pos;\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    return root;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ json_parse_file() */\njson_node_t *json_parse_file(json_arena_t *a, const char *path,\n                             int *err_line, const char **err_msg)\n{\n    FILE *fp = fopen(path, \"rb\");\n    if (!fp) {\n        if (err_msg)  *err_msg  = \"cannot open file\";\n        if (err_line) *err_line = 0;\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    fseek(fp, 0, SEEK_END);\n    long sz = ftell(fp);\n    fseek(fp, 0, SEEK_SET);\n    if (sz < 0) {\n        fclose(fp);\n        if (err_msg) *err_msg = \"cannot size file\";\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    char *buf = malloc((size_t)sz + 1);\n    if (!buf) {\n        fclose(fp);\n        if (err_msg) *err_msg = \"out of memory\";\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    size_t got = fread(buf, 1, (size_t)sz, fp);\n    fclose(fp);\n    buf[got] = '\\0';\n\n    int off = 0;\n    const char *m = NULL;\n    json_node_t *n = json_parse(a, buf, &off, &m);\n    if (!n) {\n        if (err_msg) *err_msg = m;\n        if (err_line) {\n            int line = 1;\n            for (int i = 0; i < off && i < (int)got; i++) {\n                if (buf[i] == '\\n') line++;\n            }\n            *err_line = line;\n        }\n    }\n    free(buf);\n    return n;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Accessors */\njson_kind_t json_kind(const json_node_t *n)         { return n ? n->kind : JSON_NULL; }\nint         json_is_null(const json_node_t *n)      { return n && n->kind == JSON_NULL; }\nint         json_bool_value(const json_node_t *n)   { return (n && n->kind == JSON_BOOL)   ? n->u.b : 0; }\ndouble      json_number_value(const json_node_t *n) { return (n && n->kind == JSON_NUMBER) ? n->u.n : 0.0; }\nconst char *json_string_value(const json_node_t *n) { return (n && n->kind == JSON_STRING) ? n->u.s : NULL; }\nint         json_array_size(const json_node_t *n)   { return (n && n->kind == JSON_ARRAY)  ? n->u.arr.count : 0; }\nint         json_object_size(const json_node_t *n)  { return (n && n->kind == JSON_OBJECT) ? n->u.obj.count : 0; }\n\njson_node_t *json_array_at(const json_node_t *n, int i)\n{\n    if (!n || n->kind != JSON_ARRAY) return NULL;\n    if (i < 0 || i >= n->u.arr.count) return NULL;\n    return n->u.arr.items[i];\n}\n\nconst char *json_object_key(const json_node_t *n, int i)\n{\n    if (!n || n->kind != JSON_OBJECT) return NULL;\n    if (i < 0 || i >= n->u.obj.count) return NULL;\n    return n->u.obj.keys[i];\n}\n\njson_node_t *json_object_value(const json_node_t *n, int i)\n{\n    if (!n || n->kind != JSON_OBJECT) return NULL;\n    if (i < 0 || i >= n->u.obj.count) return NULL;\n    return n->u.obj.values[i];\n}\n\njson_node_t *json_object_get(const json_node_t *n, const char *key)\n{\n    if (!n || n->kind != JSON_OBJECT || !key) return NULL;\n    for (int i = 0; i < n->u.obj.count; i++) {\n        if (strcmp(n->u.obj.keys[i], key) == 0) return n->u.obj.values[i];\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Writer — declared, body deferred */\n/* The {
  "content":"# libs/json/json.c — public surface\n\nSmall DOM JSON parser written for SoraMech, not vendored. Single\nfile plus header; arena-allocated tree, single-threaded parse, no\nmutation API on parsed trees. Two halves: a parser (implemented)\nand a streaming writer (declared; body deferred to when issue 311\nneeds it).\n\n## Lifecycle\n\n- `json_arena_t *json_arena_create(void)` — empty arena; NULL on OOM.\n- `void json_arena_destroy(json_arena_t *a)` — frees every chunk.\n- `size_t json_arena_bytes(const json_arena_t *a)` — diagnostic.\n\n## Parser\n\n- `json_node_t *json_parse(arena, src, *err_offset, *err_msg)` —\n  parse a NUL-terminated string. NULL on syntax error;\n  `*err_offset` is the byte offset, `*err_msg` is a static string.\n- `json_node_t *json_parse_file(arena, path, *err_line, *err_msg)`\n  — convenience: reads the file and parses. Reports 1-based line\n  numbers on error.\n\n## Accessors\n\n- `json_kind(n)` — `JSON_NULL` / `JSON_BOOL` / `JSON_NUMBER` /\n  `JSON_STRING` / `JSON_ARRAY` / `JSON_OBJECT`.\n- `json_is_null(n)` — convenience.\n- `json_bool_value(n)`, `json_number_value(n)`, `json_string_value(n)`.\n- `json_array_size(n)`, `json_array_at(n, i)`.\n- `json_object_size(n)`, `json_object_key(n, i)`,\n  `json_object_value(n, i)`, `json_object_get(n, key)`.\n\nAll accessors return sensible defaults on the wrong kind: `0`,\n`0.0`, `NULL`, no crash. No lock\n * ordering to worry about.\n */\n\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#include <errno.h>\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <unistd.h>\n\n__thread worker_ctx_t *pool_current_worker = NULL;\n\n/* {{{ Internal task node — singly-linked FIFO */\ntypedef struct task_node {\n    pool_action_t      fn;\n    void              *arg;\n    struct task_node  *next;\n} task_node_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Pool struct */\nstruct pool {\n    int            n_workers;\n    pthread_t     *threads;\n    worker_ctx_t  *contexts;\n\n    /* Task queue. */\n    pthread_mutex_t  q_mtx;\n    pthread_cond_t   q_cv;\n    task_node_t     *q_head;\n    task_node_t     *q_tail;\n\n    /* Active-task counter and its quiescence wait. */\n    _Atomic int      active;\n    pthread_mutex_t  quiet_mtx;\n    pthread_cond_t   quiet_cv;\n\n    /* Shutdown flag. Set by pool_destroy; checked by workers. */\n    _Atomic int      shutdown;\n\n    /* Init barrier. workers_ready is incremented by each worker\n     * after its (currently empty) per-thread setup; main thread\n     * waits for workers_ready == n_workers, then flips init_released\n     * and broadcasts. */\n    int              workers_ready;\n    int              init_released;\n    pthread_mutex_t  init_mtx;\n    pthread_cond_t   init_cv;\n};\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ default_n_workers() */\nstatic int default_n_workers(void)\n{\n    const char *env = getenv(\"SORAMECH_WORKERS\");\n    if (env && env[0]) {\n        int v = atoi(env);\n        if (v > 0) return v > POOL_MAX_WORKERS ? POOL_MAX_WORKERS : v;\n    }\n    long nproc = sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN);\n    if (nproc < 1) nproc = 1;\n    if (nproc > POOL_MAX_WORKERS) nproc = POOL_MAX_WORKERS;\n    return (int)nproc;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ worker_main() — what each worker thread runs */\nstatic void *worker_main(void *arg)\n{\n    worker_ctx_t *ctx = (worker_ctx_t *)arg;\n    pool_t       *p   = ctx->pool;\n    pool_current_worker = ctx;\n\n    /* Per-worker init point — issue 303 plugs spec->init calls here\n     * for every language the map uses. Empty for now. */\n\n    /* Increment workers_ready, notify the main thread, then park at\n     * the barrier until init_released flips. */\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->init_mtx);\n    p->workers_ready++;\n    pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->init_cv);\n    while (!p->init_released) {\n        pthread_cond_wait(&p->init_cv, &p->init_mtx);\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->init_mtx);\n\n    /* Task loop. */\n    while (1) {\n        pthread_mutex_lock(&p->q_mtx);\n        while (p->q_head == NULL && !atomic_load_explicit(&p->shutdown, memory_order_acquire)) {\n            pthread_cond_wait(&p->q_cv, &p->q_mtx);\n        }\n        /* Drain queue even after shutdown is signaled so already-\n         * spawned tasks complete. */\n        if (p->q_head == NULL) {\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->q_mtx);\n            break;\n        }\n        task_node_t *t = p->q_head;\n        p->q_head = t->next;\n        if (p->q_head == NULL) p->q_tail = NULL;\n        pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->q_mtx);\n\n        t->fn(t->arg);\n        free(t);\n\n        /* Decrement active; on transition to zero, signal the\n         * quiescence waiter. The lock is taken under the\n         * pre-check-then-recheck pattern so the waiter doesn't miss\n         * the signal even if multiple workers reach zero\n         * concurrently. */\n        int prev = atomic_fetch_sub_explicit(&p->active, 1, memory_order_acq_rel);\n        if (prev == 1) {\n            pthread_mutex_lock(&p->quiet_mtx);\n            pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->quiet_cv);\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->quiet_mtx);\n        }\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ pool_create() */\npool_t *pool_create(int n_workers)\n{\n    if (n_workers <= 0) n_workers = default_n_workers();\n    if (n_workers > POOL_MAX_WORKERS) n_workers = POOL_MAX_WORKERS;\n\n    pool_t *p = calloc(1, sizeof *p);\n    if (!p) return NULL;\n\n    p->n_workers = n_workers;\n    p->threads   = calloc((size_t)n_workers, sizeof(pthread_t));\n    p->contexts  = calloc((size_t)n_workers, sizeof(worker_ctx_t));\n    if (!p->threads || !p->contexts) goto fail;\n\n    if (pthread_mutex_init(&p->q_mtx,     NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n    if (pthread_cond_init (&p->q_cv,      NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n    if (pthread_mutex_init(&p->quiet_mtx, NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n    if (pthread_cond_init (&p->quiet_cv,  NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n    if (pthread_mutex_init(&p->init_mtx,  NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n    if (pthread_cond_init (&p->init_cv,   NULL) != 0) goto fail;\n\n    atomic_init(&p->active,   0);\n    atomic_init(&p->shutdown, 0);\n\n    for (int i = 0; i < n_workers; i++) {\n        p->contexts[i].thread_idx = i;\n        p->contexts[i].pool       = p;\n        if (pthread_create(&p->threads[i], NULL, worker_main, &p->contexts[i]) != 0) {\n            /* Tear down: flip shutdown, release any already-started\n             * workers from the barrier so they can exit. */\n            atomic_store(&p->shutdown, 1);\n            pthread_mutex_lock(&p->init_mtx);\n            p->init_released = 1;\n            pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->init_cv);\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->init_mtx);\n            pthread_mutex_lock(&p->q_mtx);\n            pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->q_cv);\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->q_mtx);\n            for (int j = 0; j < i; j++) pthread_join(p->threads[j], NULL);\n            goto fail;\n        }\n    }\n    return p;\n\nfail:\n    if (p) {\n        free(p->threads);\n        free(p->contexts);\n        free(p);\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ pool_init_barrier() */\nvoid pool_init_barrier(pool_t *p)\n{\n    if (!p) return;\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->init_mtx);\n    while (p->workers_ready < p->n_workers) {\n        pthread_cond_wait(&p->init_cv, &p->init_mtx);\n    }\n    p->init_released = 1;\n    pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->init_cv);\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->init_mtx);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ pool_spawn() */\nvoid pool_spawn(pool_t *p, pool_action_t fn, void *arg)\n{\n    if (!p || !fn) return;\n    task_node_t *t = malloc(sizeof *t);\n    if (!t) return;        /* OOM: silently drop; revisit error path */\n    t->fn   = fn;\n    t->arg  = arg;\n    t->next = NULL;\n\n    /* Increment active BEFORE enqueueing so the pop+decrement on the\n     * worker side never sees active drop below the pending-work\n     * count. */\n    atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&p->active, 1, memory_order_acq_rel);\n\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->q_mtx);\n    if (p->q_tail) p->q_tail->next = t;\n    else           p->q_head       = t;\n    p->q_tail = t;\n    pthread_cond_signal(&p->q_cv);\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->q_mtx);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ pool_wait_quiescent() */\nvoid pool_wait_quiescent(pool_t *p)\n{\n    if (!p) return;\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->quiet_mtx);\n    while (atomic_load_explicit(&p->active, memory_order_acquire) > 0) {\n        pthread_cond_wait(&p->quiet_cv, &p->quiet_mtx);\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->quiet_mtx);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ pool_n_workers() */\nint pool_n_workers(const pool_t *p)\n{\n    return p ? p->n_workers : 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ pool_destroy() */\nvoid pool_destroy(pool_t *p)\n{\n    if (!p) return;\n\n    /* If pool_init_barrier was never called (e.g. error before\n     * use), release workers from the barrier so they can exit. */\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->init_mtx);\n    if (!p->init_released) {\n        p->init_released = 1;\n        pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->init_cv);\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->init_mtx);\n\n    atomic_store_explicit(&p->shutdown, 1, memory_order_release);\n\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&p->q_mtx);\n    pthread_cond_broadcast(&p->q_cv);\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&p->q_mtx);\n\n    for (int i = 0; i < p->n_workers; i++) {\n        pthread_join(p->threads[i], NULL);\n    }\n\n    pthread_mutex_destroy(&p->q_mtx);\n    pthread_cond_destroy (&p->q_cv);\n    pthread_mutex_destroy(&p->quiet_mtx);\n    pthread_cond_destroy (&p->quiet_cv);\n    pthread_mutex_destroy(&p->init_mtx);\n    pthread_cond_destroy (&p->init_cv);\n\n    free(p->threads);\n    free(p->contexts);\n    free(p);\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

}
