{
  "content":"# libs/task-pool/pool.c — public surface\n\nSoraMech-owned thread pool. N pthread workers pulling tasks off a\nsingle FIFO queue. Designed in issue 301. The 3d-rts pool at\n`/home/ritz/programming/ai-stuff/games/3d-rts/libs/900-task-pool.h`\nwas the design reference; nothing was vendored.\n\n## Lifecycle\n\n- `pool_t *pool_create(int n_workers)` — spawns workers and parks\n  them at the init barrier. `n_workers <= 0` uses\n  `sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN)` capped at `POOL_MAX_WORKERS`\n  (16). `SORAMECH_WORKERS=N` env var overrides. NULL on\n  allocation / pthread failure.\n- `void pool_init_barrier(pool_t *p)` — blocks until every worker\n  reaches the barrier, then releases them all simultaneously.\n  One-shot; the spec-registry plug-in point sits between\n  `pool_create` and `pool_init_barrier`.\n- `void pool_destroy(pool_t *p)` — flips shutdown, drains the\n  queue, joins every worker, frees.\n\n## Submission\n\n- `void pool_spawn(pool_t *p, pool_action_t fn, void *arg)` —\n  safe from any thread, including from inside another action.\n- `void pool_wait_quiescent(pool_t *p)` — blocks until the\n  active-task counter reaches zero.\n- `int  pool_n_workers(const pool_t *p)` — count.\n\n## Worker context\n\n- `extern __thread worker_ctx_t *pool_current_worker` — set on\n  every worker before the barrier; readable from any action.\n- `worker_ctx_t.thread_idx` — 0-based worker index.\n- `worker_ctx_t.pool` — back-pointer.\n- `worker_ctx_t.handles[POOL_LANG_SLOTS]` — reserved for the\n  spec registry (issue 303).\n\n## Concurrency model\n\n- One mutex for the FIFO queue (`q_mtx`), one CV (`q_cv`) for\n  workers waiting on work.\n- Atomic active-task counter; one mutex/CV pair (`quiet_mtx`,\n  `quiet_cv`) for the quiescence waiter.\n- One mutex/CV pair (`init_mtx`, `init_cv`) for the init barrier.\n- The three pairs never nest. Lock-ordering is moot.\n\n## What's NOT here (deferred)\n\n- **Per-worker spec init** between `pool_create` and\n  `pool_init_barrier`. Lands with issue 303's spec registry.\n- **Priority queue** (issue 310): the current queue is a plain\n  singly-linked FIFO. The priority work is \"wired in, no-op\n  behaviorally\" until something distinguishes task priorities.\n- **Frame-ring scheduling / park-on-slot**: the 3d-rts pool's\n  design has these; we don't need them for the dispatch model\n  (issue 304), which always spawns tasks when inputs are ready\n  rather than parking on slot wait lists.\n\n## Related\n\n- Issue 301 — design.\n- Issue 302 — slot store, the thing tasks read and write through.\n- Issue 303 — spec registry; per-worker init hook.\n- Issue 304 — dispatch action, the function `pool_spawn`'d on\n  every task.\n- Issue 310 — priority queue (open).\n",

}

{
  "content":"/* src/008-pool-runner.c — phase 3 runner entry point.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: the C binary that loads a map directory,\n * stands up the thread pool, lets the dispatch layer run every box\n * to quiescence, and writes the JSONL run log on the way out.\n *\n * Current state: loads the graph (issue 305) and stands up the pool\n * (issue 301); the dispatch layer (issue 304) and the JSONL writer\n * (issue 311) still need to land before the runner actually runs\n * anything. Spawning + quiescence work — verifiable by running the\n * binary against tests/maps/hello.\n */\n\n#include \"010-graph-loader.h\"\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ usage() */\nstatic void usage(const char *progname)\n{\n    fprintf(stderr,\n        \"usage: %s <map-directory>\\n\"\n        \"\\n\"\n        \"Runs a SoraMech map. The map directory must contain meta.json\\n\"\n        \"and a boxes/ subdirectory.\\n\",\n        progname);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(int argc, char **argv)\n{\n    if (argc < 2 || strcmp(argv[1], \"--help\") == 0 || strcmp(argv[1], \"-h\") == 0) {\n        usage(argv[0]);\n        return (argc < 2) ? 2 : 0;\n    }\n\n    const char *map_dir = argv[1];\n\n    char *err = NULL;\n    graph_t *g = graph_load(map_dir, &err);\n    if (!g) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"load failed\");\n        free(err);\n        return 1;\n    }\n\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(0);   /* default n_workers */\n    if (!p) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"soramech-pool: cannot create thread pool\\n\");\n        graph_destroy(g);\n        return 1;\n    }\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n\n    fprintf(stderr,\n        \"soramech-pool: '%s' loaded — %d box(es), entry %s, %d worker(s)\\n\",\n        graph_name(g),\n        graph_n_boxes(g),\n        graph_entry_box_id(g) ? graph_entry_box_id(g) : \"(none)\",\n        pool_n_workers(p));\n    fprintf(stderr,\n        \"soramech-pool: dispatch layer not yet wired (issue 304); \"\n        \"quiescing with no tasks.\\n\");\n\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    graph_destroy(g);\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

{
  "content":"/* tests/301-pool-test.c — unit tests for the thread pool.\n *\n * Covers the lifecycle (create / init barrier / destroy), single-\n * and many-task spawn, quiescence, the TLS worker context, recursive\n * spawn from inside an action, and a stress race that hammers the\n * queue mutex from multiple producers.\n *\n * Designed in issue 301.\n */\n\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ Test harness */\nstatic int g_pass = 0;\nstatic int g_fail = 0;\n\n#define ASSERT(cond) \\\n    do { if (!(cond)) { \\\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } } while (0)\n\n#define RUN(name) \\\n    do { \\\n        fprintf(stdout, \"  %-44s \", #name); fflush(stdout); \\\n        if (test_##name()) { fprintf(stdout, \"ok\\n\"); g_pass++; } \\\n        else                { fprintf(stdout, \"FAIL\\n\"); g_fail++; } \\\n    } while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_create_destroy_no_tasks() */\nstatic int test_create_destroy_no_tasks(void)\n{\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) == 4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);   /* immediate — no tasks */\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_default_n_workers() */\nstatic int test_default_n_workers(void)\n{\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(0);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    /* 1..POOL_MAX_WORKERS depending on machine. */\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) >= 1);\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) <= POOL_MAX_WORKERS);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_cap_at_max_workers() */\nstatic int test_cap_at_max_workers(void)\n{\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(POOL_MAX_WORKERS + 50);\n    ASSERT(p);\n    ASSERT(pool_n_workers(p) == POOL_MAX_WORKERS);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_spawn_one() */\nstatic atomic_int g_count;\nstatic void inc_action(void *arg) { (void)arg; atomic_fetch_add(&g_count, 1); }\n\nstatic int test_spawn_one(void)\n{\n    atomic_store(&g_count, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(2);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_spawn(p, inc_action, NULL);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_count) == 1);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_spawn_many() */\nstatic int test_spawn_many(void)\n{\n    enum { N = 1000 };\n    atomic_store(&g_count, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) pool_spawn(p, inc_action, NULL);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_count) == N);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_current_worker_tls() */\nstatic atomic_int g_max_idx;\nstatic void check_worker_action(void *arg)\n{\n    (void)arg;\n    worker_ctx_t *ctx = pool_current_worker;\n    if (!ctx) return;\n    int idx = ctx->thread_idx;\n    int prev = atomic_load(&g_max_idx);\n    while (idx > prev && !atomic_compare_exchange_weak(&g_max_idx, &prev, idx)) {\n        /* retry */\n    }\n}\n\nstatic int test_current_worker_tls(void)\n{\n    atomic_store(&g_max_idx, -1);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    /* Spawn enough tasks that every worker likely picks one up. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < 256; i++) pool_spawn(p, check_worker_action, NULL);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    /* At least one worker observed a non-negative thread_idx. With\n     * 256 tasks across 4 workers we should see most/all of them. */\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_max_idx) >= 0);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_max_idx) < pool_n_workers(p));\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_recursive_spawn() */\nstatic atomic_int g_recursive;\n\nstatic void recursive_action(void *arg)\n{\n    int depth = (int)(intptr_t)arg;\n    atomic_fetch_add(&g_recursive, 1);\n    if (depth > 0) {\n        /* Spawn a child from inside the worker. */\n        pool_spawn(pool_current_worker->pool, recursive_action,\n                   (void *)(intptr_t)(depth - 1));\n    }\n}\n\nstatic int test_recursive_spawn(void)\n{\n    atomic_store(&g_recursive, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    /* depth 10 → 11 invocations (10..0). */\n    pool_spawn(p, recursive_action, (void *)(intptr_t)10);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n    ASSERT(atomic_load(&g_recursive) == 11);\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_concurrent_producers() */\nstruct producer_args { pool_t *p; int n; };\n\nstatic void *producer_thread(void *arg)\n{\n    struct producer_args *a = arg;\n    for (int i = 0; i < a->n; i++) pool_spawn(a->p, inc_action, NULL);\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nstatic int test_concurrent_producers(void)\n{\n    enum { N_PROD = 8, PER = 500 };\n    atomic_store(&g_count, 0);\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(4);\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n\n    pthread_t producers[N_PROD];\n    struct producer_args args = { p, PER };\n    for (int i = 0;   "new_string":"/* {{{ test_priority_order() */\n/* Spawn several tasks before the init barrier releases the worker,\n * then verify the dequeue order respects priority (higher first)\n * with FIFO tiebreaking at equal priority. Single-worker pool is\n * used so dequeue order maps directly to execution order. */\nstatic pthread_mutex_t g_seq_mtx = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;\nstatic int g_seq[16];\nstatic int g_seq_len;\n\nstatic void seq_action(void *arg)\n{\n    int id = (int)(intptr_t)arg;\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_seq_mtx);\n    g_seq[g_seq_len++] = id;\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_seq_mtx);\n}\n\nstatic int test_priority_order(void)\n{\n    g_seq_len = 0;\n    pool_t *p = pool_create(1);\n    ASSERT(p);\n\n    /* Queue 6 tasks BEFORE the worker is released. ids encode order\n     * of spawn; the test asserts on order of execution. */\n    pool_spawn(p, seq_action, (void *)(intptr_t)1, 0);\n    pool_spawn(p, seq_action, (void *)(intptr_t)2, 5);\n    pool_spawn(p, seq_action, (void *)(intptr_t)3, 0);\n    pool_spawn(p, seq_action, (void *)(intptr_t)4, 9);\n    pool_spawn(p, seq_action, (void *)(intptr_t)5, 5);\n    pool_spawn(p, seq_action, (void *)(intptr_t)6, -1);\n\n    pool_init_barrier(p);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(p);\n\n    /* Expected order:\n     *   4 (prio 9)\n     *   2, 5 (prio 5, FIFO)\n     *   1, 3 (prio 0, FIFO)\n     *   6 (prio -1)\n     */\n    static const int expected[] = { 4, 2, 5, 1, 3, 6 };\n    ASSERT(g_seq_len == 6);\n    for (int i = 0; i < 6; i++) ASSERT(g_seq[i] == expected[i]);\n\n    pool_destroy(p);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    printf(\"301-pool-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(create_destroy_no_tasks);\n    RUN(default_n_workers);\n    RUN(cap_at_max_workers);\n    RUN(spawn_one);\n    RUN(spawn_many);\n    RUN(current_worker_tls);\n    RUN(recursive_spawn);\n    RUN(concurrent_producers);\n    RUN(priority_order);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */",

{
  "content":"/* src/011-spec-registry.c — language spec registry, implementation.\n *\n * Scans the langs/ directory at startup, dlopens every <name>/spec.so\n * it finds, reads the exported `soramech_lang_spec` symbol, and\n * stores name + file_ext + dl handle + spec pointer. Registry stays\n * alive for the run; spec_registry_destroy walks the entries and\n * dlcloses every handle.\n *\n * Per-worker spec init (running each spec's init callback once per\n * worker thread) lives in the pool, not here — issue 301's worker_main\n * gets the hook in a follow-on. This file just produces the lookup\n * table that the hook will iterate.\n */\n\n#include \"011-spec-registry.h\"\n\n#include <dirent.h>\n#include <dlfcn.h>\n#include <stdarg.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <sys/stat.h>\n\n/* {{{ Internal entry */\ntypedef struct spec_entry {\n    void             *dl_handle;\n    const lang_spec_t *spec;\n} spec_entry_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Registry */\nstruct spec_registry {\n    int           count;\n    int           capacity;\n    spec_entry_t *entries;\n};\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ err_fmt() */\n__attribute__((format(printf, 1, 2)))\nstatic char *err_fmt(const char *fmt, ...)\n{\n    char buf[1024];\n    va_list ap;\n    va_start(ap, fmt);\n    int n = vsnprintf(buf, sizeof buf, fmt, ap);\n    va_end(ap);\n    if (n < 0) return NULL;\n    size_t len = (size_t)n < sizeof buf ? (size_t)n : sizeof buf - 1;\n    char *out = malloc(len + 1);\n    if (!out) return NULL;\n    memcpy(out, buf, len);\n    out[len] = '\\0';\n    return out;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ grow_if_needed() */\nstatic int grow_if_needed(spec_registry_t *r)\n{\n    if (r->count < r->capacity) return 0;\n    int new_cap = r->capacity ? r->capacity * 2 : 4;\n    spec_entry_t *grown = realloc(r->entries, (size_t)new_cap * sizeof(spec_entry_t));\n    if (!grown) return -1;\n    r->entries  = grown;\n    r->capacity = new_cap;\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ try_load_one() — open one langs/<name>/spec.so */\n/* Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure with *err set. Skips entries\n * that don't contain a spec.so silently (a subdirectory without a\n * built spec just means that language isn't available). */\nstatic int try_load_one(spec_registry_t *r, const char *langs_dir,\n                        const char *name, char **err)\n{\n    char path[4096];\n    int w = snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/%s/spec.so\", langs_dir, name);\n    if (w < 0 || w >= (int)sizeof path) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"spec path too long: %s/%s\", langs_dir, name);\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    struct stat st;\n    if (stat(path, &st) != 0) return 0;   /* no spec.so; silent skip */\n\n    /* RTLD_LOCAL keeps symbols from one spec from leaking into\n     * another — a spec's internal helpers shouldn't be visible to\n     * any other dlopen'd module. RTLD_NOW catches missing-symbol\n     * errors immediately rather than deferring them to the first\n     * call. */\n    void *h = dlopen(path, RTLD_NOW | RTLD_LOCAL);\n    if (!h) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"dlopen('%s') failed: %s\", path, dlerror());\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    /* dlerror's \"clear the queue\" idiom: call it once before dlsym\n     * to flush any pending error, then again after to read it. */\n    (void)dlerror();\n    const lang_spec_t *spec = dlsym(h, \"soramech_lang_spec\");\n    const char *dl_err = dlerror();\n    if (!spec || dl_err) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"'%s' is missing 'soramech_lang_spec': %s\",\n                       path, dl_err ? dl_err : \"symbol not found\");\n        dlclose(h);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    if (!spec->name || !spec->file_ext) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"'%s' exports a spec with NULL name or file_ext\", path);\n        dlclose(h);\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    if (grow_if_needed(r) != 0) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\");\n        dlclose(h);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    r->entries[r->count].dl_handle = h;\n    r->entries[r->count].spec      = spec;\n    r->count++;\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ spec_registry_load() */\nspec_registry_t *spec_registry_load(const char *langs_dir, char **err)\n{\n    if (err) *err = NULL;\n    if (!langs_dir) {\n        if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"spec_registry_load: NULL langs_dir\");\n        return NULL;\n    }\n\n    DIR *d = opendir(langs_dir);\n    if (!d) {\n        if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"cannot open langs directory '%s'\", langs_dir);\n        return NULL;\n    }\n\n    spec_registry_t *r = calloc(1, sizeof *r);\n    if (!r) {\n        closedir(d);\n        if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\");\n        return NULL;\n    }\n\n    struct dirent *e;\n    while ((e = readdir(d))) {\n        if (e->d_name[0] == '.') continue;\n        /* Probe the subdir as a directory; ignore plain files. */\n        char sub[4096];\n        int w = snprintf(sub, sizeof sub, \"%s/%s\", langs_dir, e->d_name);\n        if (w < 0 || w >= (int)sizeof sub) continue;\n        struct stat st;\n        if (stat(sub, &st) != 0 || !S_ISDIR(st.st_mode)) continue;\n\n        char *one_err = NULL;\n        if (try_load_one(r, langs_dir, e->d_name, &one_err) != 0) {\n            closedir(d);\n            spec_registry_destroy(r);\n            if (err) *err = one_err;\n            else     free(one_err);\n            return NULL;\n        }\n    }\n    closedir(d);\n    return r;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ spec_registry_destroy() */\nvoid spec_registry_destroy(spec_registry_t *r)\n{\n    if (!r) return;\n    for (int i = 0; i < r->count; i++) {\n        if (r->entries[i].dl_handle) dlclose(r->entries[i].dl_handle);\n    }\n    free(r->entries);\n    free(r);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Accessors */\nint spec_registry_size(const spec_registry_t *r)\n{\n    return r ? r->count : 0;\n}\n\nconst lang_spec_t *spec_registry_get(const spec_registry_t *r, const char *name)\n{\n    if (!r || !name) return NULL;\n    for (int i = 0; i < r->count; i++) {\n        if (strcmp(r->entries[i].spec->name, name) == 0) return r->entries[i].spec;\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nconst lang_spec_t *spec_registry_for_ext(const spec_registry_t *r, const char *file_ext)\n{\n    if (!r || !file_ext) return NULL;\n    for (int i = 0; i < r->count; i++) {\n        if (strcmp(r->entries[i].spec->file_ext, file_ext) == 0) return r->entries[i].spec;\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nconst lang_spec_t *spec_registry_at(const spec_registry_t *r, int i)\n{\n    if (!r || i < 0 || i >= r->count) return NULL;\n    return r->entries[i].spec;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

{
  "content":"/* tests/011-spec-registry-test.c — unit tests for the spec\n * registry.\n *\n * Exercises directory scan, dlopen, symbol lookup, and the name /\n * extension accessors. Uses the langs/{lua,c,bash}/spec.so stubs\n * that ship with the build, so this test only runs from the\n * project root (where `langs/` is reachable).\n */\n\n#include \"011-spec-registry.h\"\n\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <sys/stat.h>\n\n/* {{{ Test harness */\nstatic int g_pass = 0;\nstatic int g_fail = 0;\n\n#define ASSERT(cond) \\\n    do { if (!(cond)) { \\\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } } while (0)\n\n#define RUN(name) \\\n    do { \\\n        fprintf(stdout, \"  %-44s \", #name); fflush(stdout); \\\n        if (test_##name()) { fprintf(stdout, \"ok\\n\"); g_pass++; } \\\n        else                { fprintf(stdout, \"FAIL\\n\"); g_fail++; } \\\n    } while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_load_three_specs() */\nstatic int test_load_three_specs(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    spec_registry_t *r = spec_registry_load(\"langs\", &err);\n    if (!r) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      spec_registry_load failed: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"(null)\");\n        free(err);\n        return 0;\n    }\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_size(r) == 3);\n\n    /* Order isn't guaranteed (depends on readdir), but all three\n     * names must be reachable by lookup. */\n    const lang_spec_t *lua  = spec_registry_get(r, \"lua\");\n    const lang_spec_t *cspec = spec_registry_get(r, \"c\");\n    const lang_spec_t *bash = spec_registry_get(r, \"bash\");\n    ASSERT(lua  && strcmp(lua ->file_ext, \".lua\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(cspec&& strcmp(cspec->file_ext, \".c\")  == 0);\n    ASSERT(bash && strcmp(bash->file_ext, \".sh\")  == 0);\n\n    /* By extension */\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_for_ext(r, \".lua\") == lua);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_for_ext(r, \".c\")   == cspec);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_for_ext(r, \".sh\")  == bash);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_for_ext(r, \".rs\")  == NULL);\n\n    /* By unknown name */\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_get(r, \"rust\") == NULL);\n\n    /* Enumeration */\n    int seen_lua = 0, seen_c = 0, seen_bash = 0;\n    for (int i = 0; i < spec_registry_size(r); i++) {\n        const lang_spec_t *s = spec_registry_at(r, i);\n        ASSERT(s);\n        if (strcmp(s->name, \"lua\")  == 0) seen_lua  = 1;\n        if (strcmp(s->name, \"c\")    == 0) seen_c    = 1;\n        if (strcmp(s->name, \"bash\") == 0) seen_bash = 1;\n    }\n    ASSERT(seen_lua && seen_c && seen_bash);\n\n    spec_registry_destroy(r);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_missing_dir() */\nstatic int test_missing_dir(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    spec_registry_t *r = spec_registry_load(\"does/not/exist\", &err);\n    ASSERT(r == NULL);\n    ASSERT(err != NULL);\n    free(err);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_null_dir() */\nstatic int test_null_dir(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    spec_registry_t *r = spec_registry_load(NULL, &err);\n    ASSERT(r == NULL);\n    ASSERT(err != NULL);\n    free(err);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_null_safety() */\nstatic int test_null_safety(void)\n{\n    /* All accessors must tolerate NULL registry. */\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_size(NULL) == 0);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_get(NULL, \"lua\") == NULL);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_for_ext(NULL, \".lua\") == NULL);\n    ASSERT(spec_registry_at(NULL, 0) == NULL);\n    spec_registry_destroy(NULL); /* must not crash */\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    /* The langs/ directory must be reachable from cwd. */\n    struct stat st;\n    if (stat(\"langs\", &st) != 0 || !S_ISDIR(st.st_mode)) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"011-spec-registry-test: langs/ not found; \"\n                        \"run from project root\\n\");\n        return 2;\n    }\n    printf(\"011-spec-registry-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(load_three_specs);\n    RUN(missing_dir);\n    RUN(null_dir);\n    RUN(null_safety);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

```
1	# 310 — Priority queue: wired in, no-op behaviorally
2	
3	## Status
4	open
5	
6	## Current behavior
7	The SoraMech thread pool's `pool_spawn` (modeled on 3d-rts's API)
8	takes a priority parameter:
9	
10	```c
11	task_id_t pool_spawn(task_pool_t *pool,
12	                     action_fn_t  *actions,
13	                     void        **action_args,
14	                     int           n_actions,
15	                     int           priority);
16	```
17	
18	Higher priority tasks are dispatched ahead of lower priority tasks
19	when multiple are ready. The pool's queue handles the ordering.
20	
21	Phase 3 needs to specify what SoraMech does with this knob. The
22	simplest answer is the right one for now: do nothing.
23	
24	## Decision
25	
26	Every dispatch task is submitted at priority `1`. The compile-time
27	constant `MAX_PRIORITY` is set to `1`. There is no graph-level or
28	box-level concept of priority. The runner does not expose any user-
29	facing knob for it.
30	
31	The mechanism is wired through the codebase — every `pool_spawn`
32	call passes a priority, the constant is referenced rather than
33	hard-coded inline — but the behavior is identical to a single-
34	priority pool. Tasks run in submission order (modulo whatever
35	ordering the pool guarantees within a single priority level).
36	
37	## Why wire it in if it does nothing
38	
39	Two reasons:
40	
41	1. **Future hooks land as config changes, not refactors.** When a
42	   real priority use case appears (allocator cleanup at lowest
43	   priority; user-marked urgent boxes; iterator queue draining
44	   prioritized over new entry submission), raising `MAX_PRIORITY`
45	   and emitting different priorities at the right call sites is a
46	   line edit, not a structural change. If the priority parameter
47	   were stripped out, adding it later means going back through every
48	   `pool_spawn` callsite and threading a new argument.
49	
50	2. **The pool's API requires it.** `pool_spawn` takes a priority.
51	   Callers must pass something. Passing `1` consistently is the
52	   straightforward expression of "no priority concept yet."
53	
54	## Specific call sites
55	
56	```c
57	// src/dispatch.c — every dispatch task
58	pool_spawn(pool, &dispatch_action, &task_arg, 1, SM_PRIORITY_DEFAULT);
59	
60	// src/008-pool-runner.c — entry-box submission at startup
61	pool_spawn(pool, &dispatch_action, &task_arg, 1, SM_PRIORITY_DEFAULT);
62	
63	// src/slot-store.c — deferred allocator cleanup task (issue 302)
64	pool_spawn(pool, &cleanup_action, &cleanup_arg, 1, SM_PRIORITY_DEFAULT);
65	
66	// langs/bash/spec.c — ... none, the spec doesn't spawn pool tasks
67	```
68	
69	`SM_PRIORITY_DEFAULT` is `1`. Defined in `src/008-pool-runner.h` (or
70	a sibling header) so all callers use the same name.
71	
72	## Future hooks (not in scope, but called out)
73	
74	When `MAX_PRIORITY` is raised, the natural assignments are:
75	
76	| Future use case                                     | Priority |
77	|-----------------------------------------------------|----------|
78	| User-marked "urgent" boxes (UI / interactive)       | 3        |
79	| Iterator continuation when its queue is non-empty   | 2        |
80	| Default dispatch task                               | 1        |
81	| Allocator cleanup task (deferred coalescing, 302)   | 0        |
82	
83	These are speculative. The actual priority schema is decided when
84	there is a workload that demonstrates the need.
85	
86	A box-level priority field could go in the box JSON (`"priority":
87	2`) and be plumbed through `dispatch_task_t`. The dispatch action
88	reads it, passes it to `pool_spawn` for any successor tasks. This
89	is a future change.
90	
91	## Open questions
92	
93	(none currently — this is intentionally a small change to the call
94	sites. The design conversation about what priorities should mean is
95	deferred until concrete need.)
96	
97	## Suggested implementation sequence
98	
99	1. Define `SM_PRIORITY_DEFAULT` (= 1) and `SM_MAX_PRIORITY` (= 1)
100	   in a runner-wide header.
101	2. Make every `pool_spawn` call site pass `SM_PRIORITY_DEFAULT`.
102	3. Set the pool's max priority at `pool_create` time using
103	   `SM_MAX_PRIORITY` (if the pool API takes a max-priority hint).
104	4. That's it. No tests required beyond verifying the constants
105	   compile and the pool runs.
106	
107	## Relevant files
108	
109	- `src/008-pool-runner.c` — calls `pool_spawn` for entry boxes
110	- `src/dispatch.c` — calls `pool_spawn` for successor tasks
111	- `src/slot-store.c` — calls `pool_spawn` for deferred cleanup
112	- `libs/task-pool/900-task-pool.h` — `pool_spawn` priority parameter
113	- `issues/301-pool-lifecycle-and-worker-init.md` — pool lifecycle
114	- `issues/304-task-dispatch-layer.md` — dispatch task submission
115	- `issues/302-wire-value-slot-store.md` — deferred cleanup tasks
116	
```

  "new_string":"/* {{{ box_is_iterator() — true iff this is a call box whose routing\n * kind cuts cycles. Cycles passing through an iterator are\n * legitimate (the iterator's input queue eventually empties and\n * the cycle terminates); cycles that don't are deadlocks at\n * load time and must be rejected. */\nstatic int box_is_iterator(const box_t *b)\n{\n    return b->kind == BOX_CALL && b->routing.kind == ROUTING_ITERATOR;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ dfs_cycle() — recursive DFS for non-iterator cycle detection */\n/* colors: 0 = white (not seen), 1 = gray (on current stack),\n * 2 = black (finished). Returns 0 on success, -1 if a cycle was\n * found; *culprit_box is the box where the back-edge was detected. */\nstatic int dfs_cycle(const graph_t *g, int box_id, char *color,\n                     int *culprit_box)\n{\n    color[box_id] = 1;\n    const box_t *src = &g->boxes[box_id];\n\n    /* Skip outgoing edges from iterator boxes. The iterator naturally\n     * terminates on input-queue empty, so cycles that loop through\n     * one are legal. Skipping is the cleanest way to express\n     * \"this edge doesn't propagate cycle reachability.\" */\n    if (!box_is_iterator(src)) {\n        for (int i = 0; i < src->n_connections; i++) {\n            int dst = src->connections[i].to_box_idx;\n            if (color[dst] == 1) { *culprit_box = box_id; return -1; }\n            if (color[dst] == 0) {\n                if (dfs_cycle(g, dst, color, culprit_box) != 0) return -1;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    color[box_id] = 2;\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ detect_cycles() — phase 4 part 2 */\nstatic int detect_cycles(const graph_t *g, char **err)\n{\n    if (g->n_boxes == 0) return 0;\n    char *color = calloc((size_t)g->n_boxes, 1);\n    if (!color) { *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\"); return -1; }\n\n    for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n        if (color[i] != 0) continue;\n        int culprit = -1;\n        if (dfs_cycle(g, i, color, &culprit) != 0) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"non-iterator cycle detected (back-edge from \"\n                           \"box '%s'); cycles must pass through an \"\n                           \"iterator-routing box\",\n                           g->boxes[culprit].id);\n            free(color);\n            return -1;\n        }\n    }\n    free(color);\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ resolve_topology() — phase 4 (partial: endpoints only) */",

{
  "content":"/* langs/lua/spec.c — Lua language spec for SoraMech.\n *\n * Per-worker handle is a `lua_State` with the standard libraries\n * opened. Invocation convention: the box's source file is expected\n * to return a Lua table (`return M` at the bottom), and the\n * fn_name is a key into that table. Inputs arrive as byte arrays;\n * each one is pushed as a Lua string. The function's single return\n * value is converted to a string (via tostring semantics) and\n * memcpy'd into the caller's output buffer.\n *\n * Designed in issue 306. Implementation choices that matter:\n *\n *  - One lua_State per worker thread. lua_State is not\n *    thread-safe, but per-thread requires no locking.\n *  - The state's stack is rewound to its baseline depth at every\n *    invoke entry/exit so cross-call leaks don't accumulate.\n *  - File caching (luaL_loadfile once, replayed via lua_call) is\n *    deferred — this iteration loads the chunk on every invoke.\n *    Lands as a follow-on once profiling justifies it.\n *  - The chunk's side effects run on every invoke too (since\n *    we re-load and re-execute). Box source files should be pure\n *    \"return M\" modules for now.\n */\n\n#include \"lang-spec.h\"\n\n#include <lua.h>\n#include <lauxlib.h>\n#include <lualib.h>\n\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ lua_init() — create a state, open standard libs */\nstatic void *lua_init(int worker_idx)\n{\n    (void)worker_idx;\n    lua_State *L = luaL_newstate();\n    if (!L) return NULL;\n    luaL_openlibs(L);\n    return L;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ lua_teardown() */\nstatic void lua_teardown(void *handle)\n{\n    if (handle) lua_close((lua_State *)handle);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ lua_invoke() */\nstatic int lua_invoke(void *handle,\n                      const char  *file_path,\n                      const char  *fn_name,\n                      const void **input_data,\n                      const int   *input_sizes,\n                      int          n_inputs,\n                      void        *out_buf,\n                      int          out_buf_capacity,\n                      int         *out_size)\n{\n    lua_State *L = (lua_State *)handle;\n    if (!L || !file_path || !fn_name) return -1;\n\n    int baseline = lua_gettop(L);\n\n    /* Load and execute the file. Expected return: one value, a\n     * table containing the named function. */\n    if (luaL_loadfile(L, file_path) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"lua spec: loadfile('%s'): %s\\n\",\n                file_path, lua_tostring(L, -1));\n        lua_settop(L, baseline);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    if (lua_pcall(L, 0, 1, 0) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"lua spec: chunk exec '%s': %s\\n\",\n                file_path, lua_tostring(L, -1));\n        lua_settop(L, baseline);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    if (!lua_istable(L, -1)) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"lua spec: '%s' did not return a table\\n\", file_path);\n        lua_settop(L, baseline);\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    /* Pull the function out of the module table. */\n    lua_getfield(L, -1, fn_name);\n    if (!lua_isfunction(L, -1)) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"lua spec: '%s' is not a function in %s\\n\",\n                fn_name, file_path);\n        lua_settop(L, baseline);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    /* Stack now: ..., module_table, function — drop the table. */\n    lua_remove(L, -2);\n\n    /* Push each input as a Lua string. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < n_inputs; i++) {\n        if (input_data[i] == NULL && input_sizes[i] > 0) {\n            fprintf(stderr, \"lua spec: input %d is NULL with size %d\\n\",\n                    i, input_sizes[i]);\n            lua_settop(L, baseline);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        lua_pushlstring(L, (const char *)input_data[i], (size_t)input_sizes[i]);\n    }\n\n    /* Call. One return value expected. */\n    if (lua_pcall(L, n_inputs, 1, 0) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"lua spec: %s.%s: %s\\n\",\n                file_path, fn_name, lua_tostring(L, -1));\n        lua_settop(L, baseline);\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    /* Convert the return to a string. tostring handles numbers /\n     * booleans / nil; if the spec needs richer marshaling later\n     * (tables, structs), that's an issue-312-shaped change. */\n    size_t len = 0;\n    const char *result = lua_tolstring(L, -1, &len);\n    if (!result) {\n        /* Non-coercible value. For now, surface as zero-length\n         * output rather than an error — the box returned something\n         * we can't serialize, but the call itself succeeded. */\n        if (out_size) *out_size = 0;\n        lua_settop(L, baseline);\n        return 0;\n    }\n    if ((int)len > out_buf_capacity) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"lua spec: %s.%s returned %zu bytes; \"\n                        \"buffer is %d\\n\",\n                file_path, fn_name, len, out_buf_capacity);\n        lua_settop(L, baseline);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    if (out_buf && len > 0) memcpy(out_buf, result, len);\n    if (out_size) *out_size = (int)len;\n\n    lua_settop(L, baseline);\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ soramech_lang_spec */\nlang_spec_t soramech_lang_spec = {\n    .name     = \"lua\",\n    .file_ext = \".lua\",\n    .init     = lua_init,\n    .teardown = lua_teardown,\n    .compile  = 0,\n    .invoke   = lua_invoke,\n};\n/* }}} */\n",

}

  "new_string":"const lang_spec_t *spec_registry_at(const spec_registry_t *r, int i)\n{\n    if (!r || i < 0 || i >= r->count) return NULL;\n    return r->entries[i].spec;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ spec_registry_init_worker() */\nint spec_registry_init_worker(spec_registry_t *r, int worker_idx,\n                              void **handles, int handles_capacity)\n{\n    if (!r || !handles) return -1;\n    if (handles_capacity < r->count) return -1;\n\n    for (int i = 0; i < r->count; i++) handles[i] = NULL;\n\n    for (int i = 0; i < r->count; i++) {\n        const lang_spec_t *s = r->entries[i].spec;\n        if (!s->init) continue;          /* spec opts out of init */\n        void *h = s->init(worker_idx);\n        if (!h) {\n            /* Teardown anything we've already created. */\n            spec_registry_teardown_worker(r, handles, i);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        handles[i] = h;\n    }\n    return r->count;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ spec_registry_teardown_worker() */\nvoid spec_registry_teardown_worker(spec_registry_t *r,\n                                   void **handles, int n_handles)\n{\n    if (!r || !handles) return;\n    if (n_handles > r->count) n_handles = r->count;\n    /* Walk in reverse — symmetric with init order. */\n    for (int i = n_handles - 1; i >= 0; i--) {\n        const lang_spec_t *s = r->entries[i].spec;\n        if (s->teardown && handles[i]) {\n            s->teardown(handles[i]);\n        }\n        handles[i] = NULL;\n    }\n}\n/* }}} */",

Look up `box = graph_box(ctx->graph, task->box_id)`.\n *   2. For each input port: slot_peek or slot_pop into a buffer.\n *   3. Call the language spec via the per-worker handle.\n *   4. Dispatch on `box->routing.kind` to pick the output branch.\n *   5. For each firing wire: slot_push to the consumer's input\n *      slot, then run the spawn-on-input-ready check.\n *\n * Plumbing each of those onto a real graph involves the per-port\n * slot table (from issue 305's slot-class enumeration pass, still\n * deferred), per-worker spec handles (303's worker hook), and the\n * graph's resolved connection endpoints (305, done).\n */\n\n#include \"012-dispatch.h\"\n\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n\n/* {{{ dispatch_spawn() */\nvoid dispatch_spawn(const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, int box_id, int priority)\n{\n    if (!ctx || !ctx->pool) return;\n    dispatch_task_t *t = malloc(sizeof *t);\n    if (!t) return;\n    t->box_id = box_id;\n    t->ctx    = ctx;\n    pool_spawn(ctx->pool, dispatch_action, t, priority);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ dispatch_action() — skeleton */\nvoid dispatch_action(void *arg)\n{\n    dispatch_task_t *t = (dispatch_task_t *)arg;\n    if (!t) return;\n\n    /* Mutable cast — `ctx` is `const` to callers, but the diagnostic\n     * counter is the action's job. */\n    dispatch_ctx_t *ctx = (dispatch_ctx_t *)t->ctx;\n    if (ctx) {\n        atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&ctx->tasks_dispatched, 1,\n                                  memory_order_relaxed);\n    }\n\n    /* Real action body lands here:\n     *\n     *   const box_t *box = graph_box(ctx->graph, t->box_id);\n     *   read_inputs(box);\n     *   invoke_spec(box);\n     *   pick_branch(box);\n     *   push_outputs(box);\n     */\n\n    free(t);\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

}

\\\n        return 0; \\\n    } } while (0)\n\n#define RUN(name) \\\n    do { \\\n        fprintf(stdout, \"  %-44s \", #name); fflush(stdout); \\\n        if (test_##name()) { fprintf(stdout, \"ok\\n\"); 3	## Status

6	## Current behavior
7	Lua boxes today run via `drivers/lua.sh`, which spawns a fresh `luajit`
8	process per box invocation, feeds it stdin, and reads stdout. Process
9	spawn cost dominates; each call is its own fresh interpreter. There is
10	no persistent Lua state between calls.
11	
12	## Concept
13	The Lua language spec implements `lang_spec_t` (issue 303) for Lua. It
14	is the first reference implementation of the spec interface and the
15	proof that the in-process FFI model works. It is also the simplest
16	case — no compile step, no out-of-process server.
17	
18	Each worker thread gets its own `lua_State`. States are not shared.
19	Per-thread states need no locking on the call path; the state's
20	internals are only ever touched by the worker that owns it.
21	
22	`langs/lua/spec.c` is built into `langs/lua/spec.so` and loaded by
23	the pool runner via `dlopen` at startup, like any other spec.

{
  "content":"# 013-jsonl-events.c — public surface\n\nPhase 3 run-log event writer. Emits one JSON object per event,\none event per line, to a writable file.\n\n## Lifecycle\n\n- `jsonl_writer_t *jsonl_writer_open(const char *path)` — opens\n  `path` for writing (truncates). NULL on failure.\n- `void jsonl_writer_close(jsonl_writer_t *w)` — fflush+fclose,\n  free.\n\n## Event emitters\n\nEach returns 0 on success, -1 on write or encode failure.\nAll emitters are thread-safe via a per-writer mutex.\n\n- `jsonl_emit_run_start  (w, ts, map, n_workers)`\n- `jsonl_emit_task_submit(w, ts, task_id, box_id, worker_idx)`\n- `jsonl_emit_task_start (w, ts, task_id, worker_idx)`\n- `jsonl_emit_task_end   (w, ts, task_id, worker_idx, duration_us, output_size)`\n- `jsonl_emit_run_end    (w, ts, duration_us, n_tasks)`\n\nTimestamps are Unix epoch seconds as doubles, matching the\narchitecture doc.\n\n## What's NOT here (deferred)\n\n- **Slot allocator events** (`slot_alloc` / `slot_free`) under\n  `SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS=1`. The proper\n  pipeline is many producers pushing fixed-size event records\n  onto a lock-free ring while one writer thread drains and\n  serializes. fopen(full, \"rb\");\n    if (!fp) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"dispatch: data box '%s': cannot open '%s'\\n\",\n                b->id, full);\n        free(full);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    int total = 0;\n    while (total < out_capacity) {\n        size_t r = fread(out_buf + total, 1,\n                         (size_t)(out_capacity - total), fp);\n        if (r == 0) break;\n        total += (int)r;\n    }\n    fclose(fp);\n    free(full);\n    *out_size = total;\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ do_file_write_box() */\n/* Convention: inputs[0] = \"path\" (string), inputs[1] = \"text\"\n * (bytes). If the box also has a literal path, we already pushed\n * it to inputs[0] via dispatch_push_literals. */\nstatic int do_file_write_box(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, const box_t *b,\n                             int *out_size)\n{\n    char       *bufs[16]  = {0};\n    const void *datas[16] = {0};\n    int         sizes[16] = {0};\n    int failed = 0;\n    int n_present = read_inputs(ctx, b, bufs, datas, sizes,\n                                ctx->default_out_capacity, &failed);\n    int path_idx = -1, text_idx = -1;\n    for (int i = 0; i < b->n_inputs; i++) {\n        if (strcmp(b->inputs[i].name, \"path\") == 0) path_idx = i;\n        if (strcmp(b->inputs[i].name, \"text\") == 0) text_idx = i;\n    }\n    if (failed || path_idx < 0 || text_idx < 0 || path_idx >= n_present || text_idx >= n_present) {\n        for (int i = 0; i < b->n_inputs; i++) free(bufs[i]);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    /* Make NUL-terminated copy of the path. */\n    char *path = malloc((size_t)sizes[path_idx] + 1);\n    if (!path) { for (int i = 0; i < b->n_inputs; i++) free(bufs[i]); return -1; }\n    memcpy(path, datas[path_idx], (size_t)sizes[path_idx]);\n    path[sizes[path_idx]] = '\\0';\n\n    char *full = resolve_path(ctx, path);\n    free(path);\n    if (!full) { for (int i = 0; i < b->n_inputs; i++) free(bufs[i]); return -1; }\n\n    FILE *fp = fopen(full, \"wb\");\n    free(full);\n    int rc = 0;\n    if (!fp) rc = -1;\n    else {\n        size_t want = (size_t)sizes[text_idx];\n        if (fwrite(datas[text_idx], 1, want, fp) != want) rc = -1;\n        fclose(fp);\n    }\n    for (int i = 0; i < b->n_inputs; i++) free(bufs[i]);\n    *out_size = 0;\n    return rc;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ dispatch_action() — the pool action body */\nvoid dispatch_action(void *arg)\n{\n    dispatch_task_t *t = (dispatch_task_t *)arg;\n    if (!t) return;\n    dispatch_ctx_t *ctx = (dispatch_ctx_t *)t->ctx;\n    const box_t *b = graph_box(ctx->graph, t->box_id);\n\n    atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&ctx->tasks_dispatched, 1, memory_order_relaxed);\n\n    int out_size = 0;\n    int out_capacity = ctx->default_out_capacity > 0\n                        ? ctx->default_out_capacity : 4096;\n    char *out_buf = malloc((size_t)out_capacity);\n    int rc = -1;\n    if (out_buf && b) {\n        switch (b->kind) {\n            case BOX_CALL:\n                rc = do_call_box(ctx, b, out_buf, out_capacity, &out_size);\n                break;\n            case BOX_DATA:\n                rc = do_data_box(ctx, b, out_buf, out_capacity, &out_size);\n                break;\n            case BOX_FILE_WRITE:\n                rc = do_file_write_box(ctx, b, &out_size);\n                break;\n        }\n    }\n\n    if (rc == 0 && b) {\n        capture(ctx, t->box_id, out_buf, out_size);\n        /* file_write boxes don't push (they're sinks). */\n        if (b->kind != BOX_FILE_WRITE) {\n            push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_buf, out_size);\n        }\n    } else if (b) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"dispatch: box '%s' failed (rc=%d)\\n\", b->id, rc);\n    }\n\n    free(out_buf);\n    free(t);\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

10	 *   1. Load and validate the graph (305).
11	 *   2. Create the slot store (302) and spec registry (303).
12	 *   3. Create the thread pool (301) and register a per-worker
13	 *      init callback that populates each worker's handles[]
14	 *      with the spec registry (303 pool hook).
15	 *   4. Attach runtime — allocate one slot per input port and
16	 *      resolve each call box's spec (305 phase 5+7).
17	 *   5. Initialize the dispatch context with output capture.
18	 *   6. pool_init_barrier — releases workers from their init
19	 *      stage into the task loop.
20	 *   7. Push literal input values to slots, then spawn every box
21	 *      that's ready (every input either literal or optional).
22	 *      Wired-input boxes spawn automatically when an upstream
23	 *      push triggers spawn-on-ready.
24	 *   8. pool_wait_quiescent.
25	 *   9. Print each box's captured output, tear down.
26	 *
27	 * The JSONL run log (issue 311) and the dispatch action's
28	 * iterator multi-spawn path (issue 304) are still ahead.
29	 */
30	
31	#include "010-graph-loader.h"
32	#include "009-slot-store.h"
33	#include "011-spec-registry.h"
34	#include "012-dispatch.h"
35	#include "pool.h"
36	
37	#include <stdio.h>
38	#include <stdlib.h>
39	#include <string.h>
40	
41	/* {{{ usage() */
42	static void usage(const char *progname)
43	{
44	    fprintf(stderr,
45	        "usage: %s <map-directory>\n"
46	        "\n"
47	        "Runs a SoraMech map. The map directory must contain meta.json\n"
48	        "and a boxes/ subdirectory.\n",
49	        progname);
50	}
51	/* }}} */
52	
53	/* {{{ spec_pool_init_cb() */
54	/* Pool init callback that populates each worker's per-language
55	 * handles by calling spec_registry_init_worker. */
56	static int spec_pool_init_cb(int worker_idx, worker_ctx_t *ctx, void *user)
57	{
58	    spec_registry_t *r = (spec_registry_t *)user;
59	    return spec_registry_init_worker(r, worker_idx, ctx->handles,
60	                                     POOL_LANG_SLOTS) >= 0 ? 0 : -1;
61	}
62	/* }}} */
63	
64	/* {{{ print_outputs() */
65	static void print_outputs(const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx)
66	{
67	    if (!ctx->last_outputs) return;
68	    for (int i = 0; i < ctx->n_boxes; i++) {
69	        const box_t *b = graph_box(ctx->graph, i);
70	        const char *out = ctx->last_outputs[i];
71	        if (out) {
72	            fprintf(stderr, "  %s → %s\n", b->id, out);
73	        } else {
74	            fprintf(stderr, "  %s → (no output)\n", b->id);
75	        }
76	    }
77	}
78	/* }}} */
79	
80	/* {{{ main() */
81	int main(int argc, char **argv)
82	{
83	    if (argc < 2 || strcmp(argv[1], "--help") == 0 || strcmp(argv[1], "-h") == 0) {
84	        usage(argv[0]);
85	        return (argc < 2) ? 2 : 0;
86	    }
87	    const char *map_dir = argv[1];
88	    char *err = NULL;
89	    int   rc  = 1;
90	
91	    graph_t         *g     = NULL;
92	    slot_store_t    *slots = NULL;
93	    spec_registry_t *specs = NULL;
94	    pool_t          *pool  = NULL;
95	    dispatch_ctx_t   ctx;
96	    int ctx_initialised = 0;
97	
98	    /* 1. Load the graph. */
99	    g = graph_load(map_dir, &err);
100	    if (!g) {
101	        fprintf(stderr, "soramech-pool: %s\n", err ? err : "load failed");
102	        goto cleanup;
103	    }
104	
105	    /* 2. Slot store and spec registry. */
106	    slots = slot_store_create();
107	    if (!slots) {
108	        fprintf(stderr, "soramech-pool: slot_store_create failed\n");
109	        goto cleanup;
110	    }
111	    specs = spec_registry_load("langs", &err);
112	    if (!specs) {
113	        fprintf(stderr, "soramech-pool: %s\n", err ? err : "spec load failed");
114	        goto cleanup;
115	    }
116	
117	    /* 3. Pool. */
118	    pool = pool_create(0);   /* default n_workers */
119	    if (!pool) {
120	        fprintf(stderr, "soramech-pool: pool_create failed\n");
121	        goto cleanup;
122	    }
123	    pool_set_worker_init(pool, spec_pool_init_cb, specs);
124	
125	    /* 4. Attach runtime (allocate slots, resolve specs). */
126	    if (graph_attach_runtime(g, slots, specs, 4096, &err) != 0) {
127	        fprintf(stderr, "soramech-pool: %s\n", err ? err : "attach runtime failed");
128	        goto cleanup;
129	    }
130	
131	    /* 5. Dispatch context with output capture. */
132	    if (dispatch_ctx_init(&ctx, g, slots, specs, pool, 1, &err) != 0) {
133	        fprintf(stderr, "soramech-pool: %s\n", err ? err : "dispatch_ctx_init failed");
134	        goto cleanup;
135	    }
136	    ctx_initialised = 1;
137	
138	    /* 6. Barrier — workers populate handles, then enter the task loop. */
139	    if (pool_init_barrier(pool) != 0) {
140	        fprintf(stderr, "soramech-pool: worker init failed\n");
141	        goto cleanup;
142	    }
143	
144	    fprintf(stderr,
145	        "soramech-pool: '%s' — %d box(es), entry %s, %d worker(s)\n",
146	        graph_name(g), graph_n_boxes(g),
147	        graph_entry_box_id(g) ? graph_entry_box_id(g) : "(none)",
148	        pool_n_workers(pool));
149	
150	    /* 7. Push literals, then walk every box and spawn whichever
151	     *    are ready. Wired-input consumers will get auto-spawned by
152	     *    the dispatch action's spawn-on-input-ready check. */
153	    if (dispatch_push_literals(&ctx, &err) != 0) {
154	        fprintf(stderr, "soramech-pool: %s\n", err ? err : "push literals failed");
155	        goto cleanup;
156	    }
157	    for (int i = 0; i < graph_n_boxes(g); i++) {
158	        dispatch_spawn_if_ready(&ctx, i, 0);
159	    }
160	
161	    /* 8. Quiesce. */
162	    pool_wait_quiescent(pool);
163	
164	    /* 9. Report. */
165	    fprintf(stderr, "soramech-pool: run complete (%d task(s)).\n",
166	            ctx.tasks_dispatched);
167	    fprintf(stderr, "soramech-pool: outputs:\n");
168	    print_outputs(&ctx);
169	
170	    rc = 0;
171	
172	cleanup:
173	    free(err);
174	    if (ctx_initialised) dispatch_ctx_destroy(&ctx);
175	    if (pool)  pool_destroy(pool);
176	    if (specs) spec_registry_destroy(specs);
177	    if (slots) slot_store_destroy(slots);
178	    if (g)     graph_destroy(g);
179	    return rc;
180	}
181	/* }}} */
182	
```

| fixture | path | result |
|--|--|--|

| `tests/maps/hello` | data → Lua | `who → World`, `greet → Hello, World!` |

Every run writes a real `last-run.jsonl` with `run_start` / `task_start` / `task_end` / `run_end` events through the dedicated writer thread.

**Progress now:**

| Issue | Status |
|-------|--------|
| 301 | in progress · pool skeleton done |
| 302 | in progress · core complete |
| 303 | in progress · registry + per-worker init + pool hook done |
| 304 | in progress · plain-call dispatch + spawn-on-ready + multilang end-to-end |
| 305 | in progress · parse + schema + topology + cycles + slot/spec attach done |
| 306 | in progress · init + invoke + teardown done, file caching pending |

| 308 | in progress · fork+exec invoke done, persistent socket deferred |

**Highlights this round:**

- **305 runtime attach** — `graph_attach_runtime(g, slots, specs, …)` allocates one slot per input port and resolves each call box's spec by lang or by file extension. Graph also remembers `map_dir` so data/file_write boxes can resolve relative paths.
- **304 real dispatch** — full action body: read inputs via peek, invoke spec via worker handle, push outputs, fire spawn-on-input-ready CAS-guarded chaining. Handles BOX_CALL, BOX_DATA (file read), BOX_FILE_WRITE (file write).
- **311 MPSC event queue** — producers append under a brief mutex and signal a CV; writer thread snapshots the head atomically and drains outside the lock so encoding + fwrite happens with zero producer contention. 8-producer burst with 2000 events round-trips cleanly.
- **008-pool-runner integration** — full lifecycle: load, attach runtime, init barrier, push literals, spawn ready boxes, wait quiescent, emit events, report outputs.
- **307 lazy `.c → .so` compile** — if invoke gets a `.c` path, it compiles to `/tmp/soramech-c-<hash>.so` and dlopens that. Lets the pipeline fixture's `pipeline.c` "just work" without a separate compile step.
- **Five-box multilang pipeline** runs every spec type in one map.

This is the first round where phase 3 actually executes maps with real code through every spec type. Pick the next round?

  "old_string":"/* {{{ push_to_downstream() — fan output to every outgoing connection */\n/* The push triggers spawn_if_ready on the consumer. */\nstatic int push_to_downstream(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, const box_t *b,\n                              const void *out_bytes, int out_size)\n{\n    for (int i = 0; i < b->n_connections; i++) {\n        const connection_t *c = &b->connections[i];\n        if (c->to_box_idx < 0) continue;\n        const box_t *dst = graph_box(ctx->graph, c->to_box_idx);\n        if (!dst || !dst->input_slot_ids) continue;\n        if (c->to_input_idx < 0 || c->to_input_idx >= dst->n_inputs) continue;\n        if (slot_push(ctx->slots, dst->input_slot_ids[c->to_input_idx],\n                      out_bytes, out_size, 0) != 0) {\n            fprintf(stderr, \"dispatch: '%s' → '%s'.%s: push failed\\n\",\n                    b->id, dst->id, c->to_input);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        dispatch_spawn_if_ready(ctx, c->to_box_idx, 0);\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */"
}

{
  "new_string":"/* {{{ test_comparator_routing() */\n/* The comparator fixture's classify box returns its literal input\n * unchanged. With v=\"8\" and comparand=5, dispatch should route\n * along the \"gt\" branch — only high fires, low and mid don't. */\nstatic int test_comparator_routing(void)\n{\n    runtime_t rt;\n    if (runtime_setup(&rt, \"tests/maps/comparator\", 2, 1) != 0) {\n        runtime_teardown(&rt); return 0;\n    }\n    char *err = NULL;\n    ASSERT(dispatch_push_literals(&rt.ctx, &err) == 0);\n\n    int classify = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"classify\");\n    int low      = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"low\");\n    int mid      = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"mid\");\n    int high     = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"high\");\n    ASSERT(classify >= 0 && low >= 0 && mid >= 0 && high >= 0);\n\n    dispatch_spawn_if_ready(&rt.ctx, classify, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(rt.pool);\n\n    /* classify ran; only the \"gt\" branch (high) ran behind it. */\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[classify] != NULL);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[classify], \"8\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[high] != NULL);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[high], \"HIGH:8\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[low] == NULL);\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[mid] == NULL);\n\n    runtime_teardown(&rt);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_iterator_routing_single_fire() */\n/* First invocation of an iterator with counter=0 picks branch\n * out_0. Subsequent firings would advance to out_1 / out_2, but\n * this iteration's dispatch doesn't multi-spawn. */\nstatic int test_iterator_routing_single_fire(void)\n{\n    runtime_t rt;\n    if (runtime_setup(&rt, \"tests/maps/iter-route\", 2, 1) != 0) {\n        runtime_teardown(&rt); return 0;\n    }\n    char *err = NULL;\n    ASSERT(dispatch_push_literals(&rt.ctx, &err) == 0);\n\n    int iter = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"iter\");\n    int a    = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"a\");\n    int b    = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"b\");\n    int c    = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"c\");\n\n    dispatch_spawn_if_ready(&rt.ctx, iter, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(rt.pool);\n\n    /* counter=0 → out_0 → a. */\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[iter], \"hi\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[a], \"A:hi\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[b] == NULL);\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[c] == NULL);\n\n    runtime_teardown(&rt);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_iterator_routing_round_robin() */\n/* Manually spawn the iterator three times (bypassing the single-\n * spawn guard via dispatch_spawn). Each spawn picks the next\n * branch via the atomic counter; a/b/c all fire across the three\n * invocations. */\nstatic int test_iterator_routing_round_robin(void)\n{\n    runtime_t rt;\n    if (runtime_setup(&rt, \"tests/maps/iter-route\", 2, 1) != 0) {\n        runtime_teardown(&rt); return 0;\n    }\n    char *err = NULL;\n    ASSERT(dispatch_push_literals(&rt.ctx, &err) == 0);\n\n    int iter = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"iter\");\n    int a = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"a\");\n    int b = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"b\");\n    int c = graph_box_index(rt.graph, \"c\");\n\n    /* Three direct spawns; counter advances 0 → 1 → 2 → 0. */\n    dispatch_spawn(&rt.ctx, iter, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(rt.pool);\n    dispatch_spawn(&rt.ctx, iter, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(rt.pool);\n    dispatch_spawn(&rt.ctx, iter, 0);\n    pool_wait_quiescent(rt.pool);\n\n    /* a/b/c all captured an output. The \"v\" inputs are 1-cell peek,\n     * so the most-recent capture survives — that's \"A:hi\", \"B:hi\",\n     * \"C:hi\". */\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[a] != NULL);\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[b] != NULL);\n    ASSERT(rt.ctx.last_outputs[c] != NULL);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[a], \"A:hi\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[b], \"B:hi\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(rt.ctx.last_outputs[c], \"C:hi\") == 0);\n\n    runtime_teardown(&rt);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    struct stat st;\n    if (stat(\"tests/maps/calc/meta.json\", &st) != 0 ||\n        stat(\"langs/lua/spec.so\", &st) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"012-dispatch-test: fixtures or specs not built; \"\n                        \"run from project root with `make` first\\n\");\n        return 2;\n    }\n    printf(\"012-dispatch-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(dispatch_skeleton_run);\n    RUN(end_to_end_calc);\n    RUN(calc_mul);\n    RUN(dispatch_counter_burst);\n    RUN(comparator_routing);\n    RUN(iterator_routing_single_fire);\n    RUN(iterator_routing_round_robin);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */",

| `iter-route` | `a → A:hi` | iterator picks `out_0` (counter=0) |

**Progress now:**

| Issue | Status |
|-------|--------|
| 301 | in progress · pool skeleton done |
| 302 | in progress · core complete |
| 303 | in progress · registry + per-worker init + pool hook done |
| 304 | in progress · plain + comparator + iterator routing, multilang end-to-end |
| 305 | in progress · parse + schema + topology + cycles + slot/spec attach + counter slots |
| 306 | in progress · init + invoke + teardown + per-worker module cache done |

**Highlights:**
- **304 routing kinds** — `push_routed` branches on `routing.kind`. Comparator parses output as a double and picks `lt`/`eq`/`gt`; iterator reads `slot_read_inc` on its counter slot and picks `out_<idx>`. Three new fixture-driven dispatch tests verify each path including a 3-call round-robin that walks the iterator counter through all branches.
- **305 atomic counter slots** — `graph_attach_runtime` allocates a `SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER` slot for each iterator-routing box and stores its id on `box->counter_slot_id`.
- **306 Lua module cache** — per-worker `LUA_REGISTRYINDEX[LUA_CACHE_KEY]` holds module tables keyed by file path. Subsequent invokes skip `luaL_loadfile + lua_pcall` entirely. Per-worker means no locking.
- **311 task_id correlation** — `task_id` assigned at `dispatch_spawn` time and threaded through `task_submit` / `task_start` / `task_end` so the JSONL log can correlate them. The submit event has worker_idx=-1 (not yet picked up); start/end have the dispatching worker's index.

  "content":"#!/bin/bash\n# scripts/run-tests.sh — phase 3 integration tests.\n#\n# Runs every fixture map under tests/maps/ through `soramech-pool`\n# and asserts that the captured outputs match a hardcoded\n# expectation per map. The point is to catch regressions\n# end-to-end — past the spec interface, past the dispatch action,\n# past JSONL writing — rather than via the in-process unit tests.\n#\n# Per the project convention: scripts run from any directory via a\n# hard-coded ${DIR} path with an override argument; all paths are\n# relative to ${DIR}.\n\nset -u\n\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\nif [[ $# -ge 1 ]]; then\n    DIR=\"$1\"\nfi\n\ncd \"$DIR\"\n\npass=0\nfail=0\nfailures=()\n\n# {{{ check_map() — run one fixture, verify expected substrings\ncheck_map() {\n    local map=\"$1\"\n    shift\n    local expected=(\"$@\")\n\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"$map\"\n\n    local output\n    output=$(\"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map\" 2>&1)\n    local rc=$?\n\n    local missing=\"\"\n    if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then\n        missing=\"exit=$rc\"\n    fi\n    for e in \"${expected[@]}\"; do\n        if [[ \"$output\" != *\"$e\"* ]]; then\n            missing+=\"${missing:+; }missing '$e'\"\n        fi\n    done\n\n    if [[ -z \"$missing\" ]]; then\n        printf \"ok\\n\"\n        pass=$((pass + 1))\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — %s\\n\" \"$missing\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"$map: $missing\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ pipeline_output_check() — additional: the pipeline writes to disk\npipeline_output_check() {\n    local file=\"/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt\"\n    rm -f \"$file\"\n    \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\" > /dev/null 2>&1\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"pipeline file_write output\"\n    if [[ -f \"$file\" ]]; then\n        local content\n        content=$(cat \"$file\")\n        if [[ \"$content\" == \"11!\" ]]; then\n            printf \"ok\\n\"\n            pass=$((pass + 1))\n        else\n            printf \"FAIL — expected '11!', got '%s'\\n\" \"$content\"\n            fail=$((fail + 1))\n            failures+=(\"pipeline file: $content\")\n        fi\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — output file missing\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"pipeline: $file missing\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ run all fixtures\necho \"integration tests (fixture maps):\"\n\ncheck_map \"calc\" \\\n    \"add → 42\"\n\ncheck_map \"hello\" \\\n    \"who → World\" \\\n    \"greet → Hello, World!\"\n\ncheck_map \"comparator\" \\\n    \"classify → 8\" \\\n    \"high → HIGH:8\" \\\n    \"low → (no output)\" \\\n    \"mid → (no output)\"\n\ncheck_map \"iter-route\" \\\n    \"iter → hi\" \\\n    \"a → A:hi\" \\\n    \"b → (no output)\" \\\n    \"c → (no output)\"\n\ncheck_map \"pipeline\" \\\n    \"input → 5\" \\\n    \"double → 10\" \\\n    \"addone → 11\" \\\n    \"shout → 11!\"\n\npipeline_output_check\n# }}}\n\necho\necho \"  $pass passed, $fail failed\"\n\nif [[ $fail -gt 0 ]]; then\n    echo\n    echo \"  failures:\"\n    for f in \"${failures[@]}\"; do\n        echo \"    - $f\"\n    done\nfi\n\nexit $fail\n",

}

{
  "content":"#!/bin/bash\n# langs/bash/bash-server.sh — persistent bash subprocess, one per\n# worker thread, that talks to the C spec over a Unix-domain\n# socketpair connected to stdin/stdout.\n#\n# Designed in issue 308. Replaces the fork+exec-per-call model\n# with a long-lived process: process startup happens once at\n# pool init, every box invocation reuses the same bash state\n# (and the sourced module cache).\n#\n# Protocol — line-oriented, all values UTF-8:\n#\n#   Request:\n#     <n_args>\\n            (or \"QUIT\" to terminate)\n#     <file_path>\\n\n#     <fn_name>\\n\n#     <arg1>\\n              (n_args of these)\n#     <arg2>\\n\n#     ...\n#\n#   Response:\n#     <exit_status>\\n        (0 on success)\n#     <output_length>\\n      (decimal byte count, no newline at end of payload)\n#     <output_bytes>         (output_length bytes, NOT followed by \\n)\n#\n# Limitations of this iteration:\n#   - Arguments cannot contain literal newlines (line-oriented protocol).\n#   - Output is read as bytes — newlines inside the payload are fine,\n#     but trailing newlines from bash builtins like `echo` are part\n#     of the output. Box functions use `printf '%s' \"$x\"` to avoid them.\n#\n# Caching: each box file is sourced on first use and remembered in\n# the `sourced` associative array; subsequent invocations skip the\n# `source` and reuse the loaded functions. Per-worker, no locking.\n\nset -u\n\ndeclare -A sourced\n\nwhile IFS= read -r n_args; do\n    [[ \"$n_args\" == \"QUIT\" ]] && break\n\n    IFS= read -r file_path\n    IFS= read -r fn_name\n\n    args=()\n    for ((i = 0; i < n_args; i++)); do\n        IFS= read -r a\n        args+=(\"$a\")\n    done\n\n    if [[ ! -f \"$file_path\" ]]; then\n        printf '127\\n0\\n'\n        continue\n    fi\n\n    if [[ -z \"${sourced[$file_path]:-}\" ]]; then\n        # shellcheck disable=SC1090\n        if ! source \"$file_path\" 2>/dev/null; then\n            printf '126\\n0\\n'\n            continue\n        fi\n        sourced[$file_path]=1\n    fi\n\n    # Capture function output and exit status. The function name\n    # itself failing (not a callable) surfaces as exit 127.\n    if ! declare -F \"$fn_name\" >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        printf '127\\n0\\n'\n        continue\n    fi\n\n    out=$(\"$fn_name\" \"${args[@]}\" 2>/dev/null)\n    status=$?\n    n=${#out}\n    printf '%d\\n%d\\n' \"$status\" \"$n\"\n    printf '%s' \"$out\"\ndone\n",
  "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/langs/bash/bash-server.sh"
}
```

{
  "content":"/* langs/bash/spec.c — Bash language spec for SoraMech.\n *\n * Persistent-subprocess model: each worker thread spawns one bash\n * process at init() and keeps it alive for the run, communicating\n * over a Unix-domain socketpair. Every invoke writes a\n * line-oriented request to the bash side and reads a framed\n * response — orders of magnitude faster than fork+exec per call.\n *\n * Designed in issue 308. The previous iteration's fork+exec path\n * lives only in git history now; this file replaces it wholesale.\n *\n * Protocol details, including the bash-side loop, are in\n * `langs/bash/bash-server.sh`. The C side here is just enough\n * machinery to spawn the subprocess and read/write the framing.\n *\n * Limitations:\n *  - Arguments containing literal newlines are not supported in\n *    this iteration (line-oriented protocol). Most bash boxes\n *    don't need them; binary data should be base64-encoded\n *    upstream.\n *  - The protocol is single-request/single-response; a slow box\n *    serializes calls behind it on the same worker. Multi-worker\n *    pools dispatch in parallel anyway, so this is rarely\n *    the bottleneck.\n */\n\n#include \"lang-spec.h\"\n\n#include <errno.h>\n#include <fcntl.h>\n#include <signal.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <sys/socket.h>\n#include <sys/types.h>\n#include <sys/wait.h>\n#include <unistd.h>\n\n#define DEFAULT_SERVER_PATH \"langs/bash/bash-server.sh\"\n\n/* {{{ Per-worker handle */\ntypedef struct {\n    int     fd;      /* parent-side socketpair fd */\n    pid_t   pid;     /* bash subprocess */\n} bash_handle_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ server_path() — locate bash-server.sh */\n/* For now, allow override via the SORAMECH_BASH_SERVER env var; the\n * default is relative to the cwd (the project root). A more\n * polished version locates the script next to the spec.so via\n * /proc/self/exe, landing with issue 309's spec discovery work. */\nstatic const char *server_path(void)\n{\n    const char *p = getenv(\"SORAMECH_BASH_SERVER\");\n    return (p && *p) ? p : DEFAULT_SERVER_PATH;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ write_all() — write n bytes, retrying on partial writes */\nstatic int write_all(int fd, const void *buf, size_t n)\n{\n    const char *p = buf;\n    size_t left = n;\n    while (left > 0) {\n        ssize_t w = write(fd, p, left);\n        if (w < 0) {\n            if (errno == EINTR) continue;\n            return -1;\n        }\n        if (w == 0) return -1;\n        p    += w;\n        left -= (size_t)w;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ read_exact() — read exactly n bytes from fd */\nstatic int read_exact(int fd, void *buf, size_t n)\n{\n    char *p = buf;\n    size_t left = n;\n    while (left > 0) {\n        ssize_t r = read(fd, p, left);\n        if (r < 0) {\n            if (errno == EINTR) continue;\n            return -1;\n        }\n        if (r == 0) return -1;\n        p    += r;\n        left -= (size_t)r;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ read_line() — read up to cap bytes including a trailing \\n */\n/* Returns the number of bytes read (including the newline), or -1\n * on error / EOF. The newline is overwritten with '\\0' so the\n * line is a NUL-terminated C string of length (return-1). */\nstatic int read_line(int fd, char *buf, int cap)\n{\n    int n = 0;\n    while (n < cap - 1) {\n        char c;\n        ssize_t r = read(fd, &c, 1);\n        if (r < 0) {\n            if (errno == EINTR) continue;\n            return -1;\n        }\n        if (r == 0) return -1;\n        if (c == '\\n') {\n            buf[n] = '\\0';\n            return n + 1;\n        }\n        buf[n++] = c;\n    }\n    buf[n] = '\\0';\n    return -1;     /* line longer than buffer */\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ bash_init() — spawn the subprocess */\nstatic void *bash_init(int worker_idx)\n{\n    (void)worker_idx;\n    int sv[2];\n    if (socketpair(AF_UNIX, SOCK_STREAM, 0, sv) != 0) return NULL;\n\n    pid_t pid = fork();\n    if (pid < 0) {\n        close(sv[0]); close(sv[1]);\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    if (pid == 0) {\n        /* Child: route the child-side socket fd to stdin+stdout. */\n        close(sv[0]);\n        if (dup2(sv[1], STDIN_FILENO)  < 0) _exit(126);\n        if (dup2(sv[1], STDOUT_FILENO) < 0) _exit(126);\n        close(sv[1]);\n\n        /* Ignore SIGPIPE so the parent dying doesn't immediately\n         * kill us — let the read on stdin return EOF and exit cleanly. */\n        signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_IGN);\n\n        execlp(\"bash\", \"bash\", server_path(), (char *)NULL);\n        _exit(127);\n    }\n    /* Parent. */\n    close(sv[1]);\n    bash_handle_t *h = malloc(sizeof *h);\n    if (!h) { close(sv[0]); return NULL; }\n    h->fd  = sv[0];\n    h->pid = pid;\n    return h;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ bash_teardown() — graceful shutdown */\nstatic void bash_teardown(void *handle)\n{\n    if (!handle) return;\n    bash_handle_t *h = (bash_handle_t *)handle;\n    /* Send \"QUIT\" so the bash loop exits cleanly; then close the\n     * socket and wait for the child. */\n    if (h->fd >= 0) {\n        (void)write_all(h->fd, \"QUIT\\n\", 5);\n        close(h->fd);\n    }\n    if (h->pid > 0) {\n        int status = 0;\n        /* Give the child a chance to exit on its own; if it doesn't,\n         * SIGTERM it. The waitpid loop handles EINTR. */\n        for (int tries = 0; tries < 200; tries++) {\n            pid_t r = waitpid(h->pid, &status, WNOHANG);\n            if (r == h->pid) goto done;\n            if (r < 0 && errno != EINTR) break;\n            struct timespec ts = { 0, 5 * 1000 * 1000 };  /* 5 ms */\n            nanosleep(&ts, NULL);\n        }\n        kill(h->pid, SIGTERM);\n        waitpid(h->pid, &status, 0);\n    }\ndone:\n    free(h);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ send_request() — write the request frame */\nstatic int send_request(int fd, const char *file_path, const char *fn_name,\n                        const void **input_data, const int *input_sizes,\n                        int n_inputs)\n{\n    char header[64];\n    int n = snprintf(header, sizeof header, \"%d\\n\", n_inputs);\n    if (n < 0 || n >= (int)sizeof header) return -1;\n    if (write_all(fd, header, (size_t)n)              < 0) return -1;\n    if (write_all(fd, file_path, strlen(file_path))   < 0) return -1;\n    if (write_all(fd, \"\\n\", 1)                        < 0) return -1;\n    if (write_all(fd, fn_name, strlen(fn_name))       < 0) return -1;\n    if (write_all(fd, \"\\n\", 1)                        < 0) return -1;\n    for (int i = 0; i < n_inputs; i++) {\n        if (write_all(fd, input_data[i], (size_t)input_sizes[i]) < 0) return -1;\n        if (write_all(fd, \"\\n\", 1) < 0) return -1;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ bash_invoke() */\nstatic int bash_invoke(void *handle,\n                       const char  *file_path,\n                       const char  *fn_name,\n                       const void **input_data,\n                       const int   *input_sizes,\n                       int          n_inputs,\n                       void        *out_buf,\n                       int          out_capacity,\n                       int         *out_size)\n{\n    if (!handle || !file_path || !fn_name) return -1;\n    bash_handle_t *h = (bash_handle_t *)handle;\n\n    if (send_request(h->fd, file_path, fn_name,\n                     input_data, input_sizes, n_inputs) != 0) {\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    /* Response: status\\n out_len\\n out_bytes. */\n    char line[64];\n    if (read_line(h->fd, line, sizeof line) < 0) return -1;\n    int status = atoi(line);\n\n    if (read_line(h->fd, line, sizeof line) < 0) return -1;\n    int n = atoi(line);\n\n    if (n > out_capacity) {\n        /* Drain the output to keep the protocol synced, then fail. */\n        char drop[1024];\n        int left = n;\n        while (left > 0) {\n            int chunk = left < (int)sizeof drop ? left : (int)sizeof drop;\n            if (read_exact(h->fd, drop, (size_t)chunk) < 0) return -1;\n            left -= chunk;\n        }\n        fprintf(stderr, \"bash spec: %s:%s returned %d bytes; ### [1842] type=assistant
ts: 2026-05-15T23:28:08.315Z

Real bug — the parent-side socketpair fds leak into other workers' forks (since worker threads concurrently fork bash). The orphan bash processes inherit each other's parent-side fds, so EOF never arrives. Fix: `SOCK_CLOEXEC`.

**Highlights this round:**

- **308 persistent bash subprocess** — replaced fork+exec-per-call with one long-lived bash subprocess per worker, talking over a `socketpair(AF_UNIX, SOCK_STREAM | SOCK_CLOEXEC)`. Line-oriented protocol: `n_args / file_path / fn_name / args` request, `status / out_len / out_bytes` response. `bash-server.sh` runs the loop and caches sourced files per worker (the bash analogue of 306's Lua module cache). All five bash-spec tests pass against the new model.

- **The CLOEXEC bug** — without `SOCK_CLOEXEC`, concurrent worker forks would inherit each other's parent-side fds and the bash subprocesses would never see EOF. Fixed at socket creation.

- **301 per-worker teardown hook** — `pool_set_worker_teardown(p, cb, user)` runs the symmetric counterpart to `pool_set_worker_init` right before each worker exits. The runner uses it to call `spec_registry_teardown_worker`, which `QUIT`s bash, closes its socket, and `waitpid`s with a 1s short-poll fallback to `SIGTERM`. **Verified zero orphan bash processes after a `soramech-pool` run.**

The bash spec is now properly out-of-process at the speed the architecture intended. Want another round?

**Highlights this round:**

- **305 language enumeration** — `graph_attach_runtime` walks every call box and stores the distinct lang names on the graph. Accessors `graph_n_languages` / `graph_language`.
- **303 language-filtered worker init** — new `spec_registry_init_worker_filtered(r, idx, handles, cap, langs, n_langs)`. The pool runner passes the map's language list so a Lua-only map's workers skip the bash subprocess spawn entirely. **calc dropped from 13ms to 1.7ms.**
- **309 spec discovery via `/proc/self/exe`** — `find_langs_dir()` checks `SORAMECH_LANGS_DIR`, then `dirname(/proc/self/exe)/langs`, then falls back to `langs` relative to cwd. Means the binary can be installed anywhere.
- **311 `SORAMECH_LOG_VALUES=1` opt-in** — dispatch now emits `task_input` (per port) and `task_output` events with the actual byte payload, truncated to 4 KB. A run with verbose logging shows:

With\n     * our current specs (which all leave invoke_native NULL), the\n     * fallback runs and behaviour is unchanged — but the\n     * infrastructure is in place for future specialisation. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n        box_t *b = &g->boxes[i];\n        if (b->kind != BOX_CALL || !b->lang) {\n            b->use_native_invoke = 0;\n            continue;\n        }\n        b->use_native_invoke = 1;\n        /* Check outgoing connections: every call-box consumer must\n         * share my language. */\n        for (int j = 0; j < b->n_connections && b->use_native_invoke; j++) {\n            int dst = b->connections[j].to_box_idx;\n            if (dst < 0) continue;\n            const box_t *c = &g->boxes[dst];\n            if (c->kind != BOX_CALL) continue;\n            if (!c->lang || strcmp(c->lang, b->lang) != 0) {\n                b->use_native_invoke = 0;\n            }\n        }\n        if (!b->use_native_invoke) continue;\n        /* Check incoming: every call-box producer feeding any of\n         * my inputs must share my language. */\n        for (int p = 0; p < g->n_boxes && b->use_native_invoke; p++) {\n            const box_t *prod = &g->boxes[p];\n            for (int k = 0; k < prod->n_connections && b->use_native_invoke; k++) {\n                if (prod->connections[k].to_box_idx != i) continue;\n                if (prod->kind != BOX_CALL) continue;\n                if (!prod->lang || strcmp(prod->lang, b->lang) != 0) {\n                    b->use_native_invoke = 0;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /* Enumerate distinct languages used by call boxes.
